New England visits Chicago at Soldier Field on Thursday, Oct. 22, at 8:15 p.m. ET, with the Bears as the 3.5-point favorites and the total at 50.5. My Patriots vs. Bears prediction backs the Over to kick off this week's NFL picks . TOP Pick Patriots vs Bears prediction: Over 50.5 The Chicago Bears have scored 59 and 31 points in Caleb Williams ' two full games, and he looked downright surgical on Sunday in Atlanta, completing an insane 30 of 36 pass attempts. The New England Patriots ' offense has been enduring a tale of two halves this season. The unit was awful through its first three games, and it then averaged 33.3 points over its next three. Drake Maye has thrown 10 touchdowns against one interception during the latter stretch. Yes, New England's offensive-line injuries concern me, but the makeshift unit didn't surrender a sack against the Jets. Now Maye gets a Chicago defense tied for last in yards allowed per play. As Jason Logan points out in his Patriots vs Bears prop picks , Chicago uses man coverage at the league's second-highest rate, a matchup that should benefit A.J. Brown. Expect the Patriots to land some haymakers. The Bears can punch back with Williams healthy, another reason he's a part of our Patriots vs. Bears touchdown picks . New England's defense was already stomped for 35 points at Jacksonville, and it surrendered 26 at Buffalo . Expect a shootout as Maye and Williams battle for bragging rights as the best quarterback from the 2024 draft class. Patriots vs Bears combo Williams' return puts some venom back into Chicago's offense. And on the other side New England has piled up 100 points during its three-game winning streak . I'm expecting sustained drives and enough end-zone visits to clear 50.5. Give me the Patriots +3.5 in a competitive game. Their season-long yards-per-play differential is positive, while Chicago's is negative. Getting more than a field goal with this version of Maye works for me. Finally, Maye has fired 10 touchdown passes over his last three games. Chicago just allowed three to Michael Penix Jr. after giving up two to Jordan Love the previous week. This Bears' secondary is starting to get badly exposed. Patriots +3.5 Drake Maye 2+ touchdown passes Patriots vs Bears touchdown scorer: DeMario Douglas DeMario Douglas and Maye are quietly building excellent chemistry while connecting for three touchdowns over the past two games. Douglas has also turned four red-zone targets this season into two scores . His touchdowns against Las Vegas came from 35 and eight yards out, so we don't need him to break off a chunk play to cash this prop, although I'll happily take one. Early Patriots vs Bears spread pick: Bears -2.5 The Chicago Bears and New England Patriots were both victorious in Week 6, but neither looked like world beaters. Chicago benefited from multiple blunders by Atlanta and still had to sweat it out in the fourth quarter. New England escaped the Jets but didn't cover at home, thanks to New York stubbing its toe on crucial fourth downs. Prime-time pups have been the trendy play over the past few weeks, but I'm not convinced the Patriots can compete in the Bears' weight class, at least on offense. All eyes are on RB2 Kyle Monangai, who has missed time with turf toe. Chicago's ground game is underrated and can get after a Pats run defense that's been pushed around. England Patriots (4-2) visit the Chicago Bears (4-2) at Soldier Field. The Patriots are on a three-game winning streak over the Bills (29-26), Raiders (47-17), and Jets (26-19). The Bears went 2-1 without Caleb Williams and got him back in a 31-23 win in Atlanta on Sunday Night Football. Chicago scored on its first drive of the game and never looked back. The Bears jumped out to a 21-7 halftime lead over Atlanta and finished the game with 386 yards to the Falcons’ 257. Both teams averaged at least 5.0 yards per play and Atlanta gave up on the run game as they ran a NFL season-low 12 times against Chicago. Establishing the lead then having a positive game script made life easy for Caleb Williams in his return. Williams recorded a career-high 83.3 completion percentage on 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a touchdown. Both quarterbacks will see a lot of man coverage on Thursday night. New England ranks third in man coverage (31.2%) and Williams ranks top 10 across the board against man. On the other side, Chicago’s defense runs man coverage 31.9%, ranking second-highest and Drake Maye ranks 33rd or worse in passer rating, completion percentage, and more against man. Oddsmakers set Chicago as a 3-point home favorite with a high game total of 50.5. New England did a lot of damage on third down against the Jets. Drake Maye and the Pats offense converted 8-of-15 third downs and Maye tossed two of his three touchdowns on third and goal. New England continued the Jets first half woes for the two minute drill as Maye led a 47-yard drive on 12 plays to go up 17-3 at the half. New England ran 148 yards on 46 carries and averaged for 4.1 yards per carry. We cane expect the Pats to establish a ground game against a Bears defense that is bottom five in yards before contact on run plays. We should also expect a bigger day from A.J. Brown who had three drops and another miscue that left his debut a disappointment. Brown finished with three receptions for 27 yards on 10 targets. If he gets 10 targets against Chicago, expect at least triple the yardage. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. picks.headline: Steelers vs. Saints Week 7 tracker: Injury updates, predictions, storylines and more
picks.blurb: The Pittsburgh Steelers will make NFL history this week, as will their opponent, the New Orleans Saints. For the first time in the league's long existence, a regular season game will be played in France. Paris, to be exact. After nearly 20 years since the Dolphins and Giants played the first regular season game outside of North America, the NFL's international footprint grows larger every year. As interesting as all of that is, the football played on the field is what really matters. Pittsburgh enters Week 7 with a 4-2 record, barely beating the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime a week ago. The Saints, meanwhile, climbed to 2-4 after a bizarre 34-27 win over the Giants. Both teams have plenty of flaws they are hoping to correct as the season goes on, but the Steelers are favored for a reason. As the game approaches, we will have all of the important details you need to know. Injury reports, weather reports, how to watch, storylines, and more. So bookmark this page and come back throughout the week! How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints in Week 7 Date: Sunday, October 25 Time: 9:30 a.m. EST TV Network: NFL Network Announcers: Dave Pasch (Play-by-Play), Kurt Warner and Jason Kelce (Color Analysts), Molly McGrath (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 7 Steelers injury reports will appear here as they become available New Orleans Saints Injury Report for Week 7 Saints injury reports will appear here as they become available Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints Week 7 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: TBD Wind Speed: TBD Precipitation: TBD Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 7 Will the Steelers continue leaning on the passing game despite missing multiple playmakers? Despite missing multiple receivers heading into their Week 6 matchup with the Buccaneers, the Steelers chose to make the passing game the focal point of the offense. While they ultimately came away with the victory, it was an ugly mess for much of the contest. Aaron Rodgers put up a solid 253 yards through the air, but it took him a whopping 49 pass attempts to get there. He was the definition of a checkdown merchant , with just five of those 49 passes traveling beyond 10 yards, according to Next Gen Stats . It seemed as though Mike McCarthy didn't have faith that Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle could succeed against the Buccaneers' stout run defense. Still, the Steelers can't win games against good teams with that offensive approach. The Saints could be a team that they can once again get away with it against, but it's something to monitor. Which team will handle the international trip better? There has been plenty of discourse surrounding how to handle playing across the pond ever since the NFL's International Series took shape. We saw the Rams be criticized for arriving in Australia right before their Week 1 disaster against the 49ers, who had been down under for days at that point. In the Steelers case, they are taking the route of trying to make the week feel as normal as possible, choosing to fly out on Thursday evening. Meanwhile, the Saints arrived in France on Monday, so they will be well adjusted by game time on Sunday. Will the contrasting strategies make any difference? Only time will tell. Can the Steelers pass rush come alive against a struggling Saints offensive line? The Steelers' pass rush has long been the strength of their defense, but they haven't been as effective on a down-to-down basis this season. According to Sumer Sports , Pittsburgh ranks just 23rd in pressure percentage at 37.4%. They do rank ninth in sacks with 16, so they have managed to get the QB on the ground at an above-average level. Still, they aren't causing as much disruption as they need to be, considering the names in that group. T.J. Watt has cooled off after a hot start, Alex Highsmith isn't having his best season, and Nick Herbig has made splash plays but hasn't been as dominant as he was last season. The interior has been hot and cold, with Cam Heyward remaining a consistent presence while the other pieces have been hit-or-miss. With the Saints missing star left tackle Kaleb Banks, this is an opportunity for them to really hit their stride. If they don't, it may be time to worry. picks.headline: Steelers vs. Saints bold predictions for NFL London game in Week 7
picks.blurb: The New Orleans Saints face the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday in an overseas Week 7 game between two teams heading in different directions. Pittsburgh is 4-2 after a 26-19 overtime win over Tampa Bay, while New Orleans is 2-4 after beating the Giants 34-27. Kickoff is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET. With both teams coming off big wins in Week 6, let’s take a look at the matchup and the bold predictions for Week 7 in Paris, France. Chris Boswell kicks five field goals, two from 50-plus Boswell is 13-for-17 on field goals this season, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) New Orleans allows 29.7 points and 377.7 yards per game. Those numbers suggest Pittsburgh will move the ball. Some of those drives will stall before the end zone, and that is where Boswell scores. The prediction goes beyond another solid outing. Boswell makes five field goals, including two from beyond 50 yards. The limitation is his four misses this season, which show he is not automatic from long range. Tyler Shough throws two interceptions Shough has a 12:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio through six games. He threw only 144 yards against the Giants, though he scored four touchdowns in total. He is also playing through broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which may explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks. Predicting two interceptions means Shough nearly matches his early-season total in one afternoon. The route to that outcome is straightforward. Pittsburgh’s lead will push New Orleans into longer passing situations, and an injured hand makes tight-window throws harder. The call is that one pass is tipped and picked off in the second half, while another is forced into coverage on a late drive. Those turnovers would turn a competitive game into a Steelers cushion. There is a counterpoint. Shough has produced touchdowns despite modest yardage, so this prediction depends on game script more than on his recent efficiency. Chris Olave posts 120 yards and two touchdowns in a losing rally Olave had double-digit targets in each of the first four games. Over the last two he has seen only 13 targets, producing an 8-89-1 line. That drop in volume looks like the sort of dip that corrects itself. Pittsburgh’s defense will give him room to correct it. New Orleans’ opponents have averaged 256.0 passing yards per game, which suggests quarterbacks can find openings in this matchup. Rookie Germie Bernard’s 11-catch, 87-yard, one-touchdown game against the Steelers’ last opponent shows how that kind of volume can arise. Olave reaches 10 targets, 120 yards and two touchdowns as New Orleans chases points. Those scores help the Saints cut a two-score deficit to three points late in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh still holds on. The prediction is Steelers 31, Saints 27, with Boswell’s late field goal sealing it. If Jordyn Tyson makes his debut after traveling with the team while recovering from a hamstring injury, the Saints’ receiving group could be even more dangerous. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. away.headline: Injury Emerges for Steelers Defensive Lineman
away.blurb: Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day popped up on the injury report, as the veteran did not practice on Wednesday due to a triceps injury. Injury Emerges for Steelers Defensive Lineman - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Injury Emerges for Steelers Defensive Lineman Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day takes part in an OTA practice on May 29, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Chris Ward Wed, October 21, 2026 at 11:07 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Joseph-Day has recorded 10 total tackles (three solos) and one fumble recovery through six games this season. Joseph-Day's fumble recovery off Derrick Harmon 's strip sack on Joe Burrow sealed a Steelers' win over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3. The Steelers are already thin on the defensive line with Harmon on injured reserve with a knee injury. Joseph-Day 's status will be something to monitor heading into Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints. Joseph-Day, who stands at 6-foot-4, 310 pounds, is in his eighth NFL season. He has spent time with the Los Angeles Rams (2019-21), Los Angeles Chargers (2022-23), San Francisco 49ers (2023) and Tennessee Titans (2024-25). He recorded 44 tackles in 2024, with three tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, six quarterback hits and a pass defended. Last season, he had 41 tackles, six tackles for loss, two sacks, six quarterback hits and a fumble recovery. Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Joseph-Day is very versatile, playing nose tackle, three-technique defensive tackle and defensive end. "I think, honestly, it's me not boxing myself in," Joseph-Day said about his versatility. "From the start, the beginning of my career, I played a lot of nose next to Aaron Donald, then when I left the Rams, we kinda had a need. We had one of our D-tackles that they signed get hurt, so they were like, 'Hey, can you play this three?' I was like, 'Whatever the team needs me to do.' And I did it, and I just didn't box myself in. "Whenever I went to Tennessee, there was (T'Vondre) Sweat. Sweat is like 360 pounds, he's a big man. So obviously he couldn't play four or five, so it was a no-brainer. Jeff (Simmons) was a three, and I was like, 'I'll play the five. I'll play the six. I'll play the four.' … Just being (able) to adapt and take pride in being that guy to whatever you need me to do, I'll be that (Swiss Army) knife." picks.blurb: Morris is surely equipped to counter Atlanta's attack, having led the same core from 2024-25 as head coach. But a San Francisco defense that tops the league in defensive expected points added per play on rushing attempts will be in for its stiffest test yet against the All-Pro ball carrier. On the other side of the ball, Brock Purdy will look to maintain sky-high efficiency despite mounting attrition at wide receiver . Falcons vs 49ers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: 49ers -4.5 Moneyline: 49ers -230; Falcons +190 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Falcons vs 49ers USA TODAY expert picks Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: 49ers 35, Falcons 24 How San Francisco's surprising defense handles Robinson is sure to be one of the most compelling storylines in this game. But mitigating any damage might not fall on that unit alone. Chicago managed to minimize Robinson's role by stringing together long drives and holding onto the ball for more than 40 minutes. Given how prolific San Francisco's offense is at working the intermediate area - and how badly Atlanta's defense struggles in that area - the 49ers could leave the Falcons in a problematic position by racing out to an early lead and controlling the terms of the game. Adam Kaufman: 49ers 30, Falcons 23 At some point, San Francisco's injuries have to catch up with it, right? The 49ers keep answering that question with another win to stay unbeaten, although Mike Evans' latest injury creates another challenge on a short week before traveling to Atlanta. Fortunately, Brock Purdy still has Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle to help keep the offense moving. I like those options against a Falcons secondary that has struggled. The Falcons' path is straightforward: feed Bijan Robinson, keep Purdy watching and prevent Michael Penix Jr. from having to rescue the game with difficult throws. That should keep Atlanta competitive, but I'm still expecting San Francisco to execute more consistently and take advantage of a mistake or two. away.headline: 49ers linked to Pro Bowl pass-rusher amid mounting injury issues
away.blurb: Bosa can return any week now, but the 49ers have been bracing to be without him for several weeks after he suffered a calf injury during warm-ups a few weeks ago. “Considering how important pressure is in the modern NFL, especially against the elite passers teams inevitably come up against in the playoffs, the Niners would be wise to bolster their edge-rushing unit with one of the best available free agents: Joey Bosa. The San Francisco 49ers may just be the best team in the NFL , but their mounting injury issues will catch up to them eventually. The team’s wide receiver corps has been ravaged in recent weeks with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Demarcus Robinson all going down with various ailments. The defensive side of the ball has also been hit hard by the injury bug as well. Defensive tackles Alfred Collins, CJ West, Sam Okuayinonu, edge-rushers Nick Bosa and Mikail Kamara, linebackers Nick Martin and Garret Wallow, cornerback Nate Hobbs, and safeties Marques Sigle and Darrick Forest are all either on injured reserve or have missed several weeks with their respective injuries. In the meantime, Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay believes San Francisco should add to its pass-rush pool by signing a five-time Pro Bowler who’s quite familiar with one of the team’s top players. “While San Francisco features a top-five defense, it hasn’t generated pressure on a consistent basis,” Kay wrote . “An extended absence from top edge-rusher Nick Bosa — who has been dealing with a calf injury since Week 2 — has hindered the team’s ability to get after opposing quarterbacks. “… Even at the age of 31 with a history of injury, Joey Bosa can still be a force. He tallied five sacks, nine tackles for a loss, 16 quarterback hits and a league-leading five forced fumbles in 15 games with the Buffalo Bills last year and could be a key rotational piece for San Francisco in the back half of 2026.” ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported weeks ago that Joey Bosa was leaning toward retirement, but that doesn’t mean he can’t be tempted to play again in the right situation. Playing with his brother on a Super Bowl frontrunner where he won’t be relied on to play every down could be that perfect storm of temptation for him. home.headline: The Atlanta Falcons Get Positive Injury News Ahead Of Hosting The 49ers
home.blurb: Middle linebacker Divine Deablo suffered an arm injury while linebacker Kendal Daniels suffered a neck injury that was severe enough to bring out the transport cart. As bleak as things looked on Sunday it was great to hear some good injury news Wednesday. Another bright spot was linebacker Daniels returning to practice. His injury on Sunday afternoon was a scary one. He was on the field for several moments and the cart was brought out to move him from the field instead of him being able to walk off on his own. He was transported to Grady Memorial Hospital for evaluation. Luckily, he was able to return to Mercedes-Benz Stadium after the game and was seen walking on his own. With Deablo not at practice, it is a good sign for the Falcons to have at least one of the linebackers return from injury. The Atlanta Falcons entered Sunday’s game against the Chicago Bears already missing cornerbacks A.J. Terrell Jr. and C.J. Henderson as well as edge rushers Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr. due to injury or suspension. During Sunday’s game, two more defensive players exited the game. Cornerback Terrell Jr. was back at practice after being placed on injured reserve with a groin injury he suffered in Week Two against the Carolina Panthers . It has been a long four weeks without Terrell Jr. for the Falcons, especially since they also lost his replacement Henderson to a groin injury. It is unlikely that Terrell Jr. will play this week against the undefeated, San Francisco 49ers . Atlanta still has time to activate Terrell Jr. to the 53-man roster and he has yet to be confirmed for Sunday. The Falcons secondary may still rely on Terrell Jr.’s younger brother, Avieon Terrell and Mike Hughes for another week. Atlanta’s secondary could definitely use his ability to defend passes and force fumbles. Week Eight could bring the first view of the Terrell brothers at corner together. The Falcons defense have been unable to contend with mobile quarterbacks and have had a hard time getting teams off the field. They will need all hands on deck as the undefeated 49ers come to town. The status of Terrell Jr. and Daniels are great signs leading into Sunday, but the questions around Deablo’s availability is concerning.

picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7
picks.blurb: The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. Deshaun Watson and Todd Monken have spoke highly of Jeudy this past week and he seems poised for another boost to his role. In Week 7 against he Titans, he can take advantage of their poor secondary and find the endzone for the first time this season. Browns secure at least five sacks Titans quarterback Cam Ward has had a rough start to the season and it has Tennessee sitting with a record of 1-5. He has a tendency to hold onto the ball, be reckless with it, and I think that has the Browns poised to have a big week on the defensive side of the ball. You cannot always count on turnovers, but you can count on Mike Rutenberg being aggressive on defense. One way he will do that is by getting after Ward, and I think that is where the Browns are most productive in the form of securing at least five sacks. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Cleveland Browns, matchups, prediction NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: Can the Tennessee Titans win twice in a row? That’s no small feat for an organization that hasn’t won consecutive games since 2022. But Tennessee’s 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts in NFL Week 6 quieted the storm after an 0-5 start. Now, the Titans (1-5) can prove it wasn’t a fluke when it hosts the Cleveland Browns (4-2) at Nissan Stadium on Oct. 25 (noon CT, CBS). Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. The Browns are 1.5-point favorites. They lost last year's meeting 31-29 after Tennessee running back Tony Pollard rushed for a career-high 161 yards and two touchdowns. Questions remain for quarterback Cam Ward and the Titans' offense, who were bailed out by the defense and special teams against the Colts . Ward’s 11 completions and 102 yards passing against the Colts were career lows, and Tennessee still ranks last in the NFL in yards per game (236.3) and tied for last in points per game (14.0). Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Browns. More: Tennessee Titans release DL Jordan Elliott after reviewing 'incident' at team facility More: Indianapolis Colts fire GM Chris Ballard after loss to Titans One Cleveland Browns stat to know Other than the Baltimore Ravens ’ opening touchdown drive last week, the Browns surrendered three points and 169 yards of total offense to finish a 13-10 victory. Cleveland hasn’t been atop the AFC North this late in the season since 2014. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Browns Tennessee spent offseason resources beefing up its pass rush for coach Robert Saleh’s defensive scheme. The results finally surfaced with six sacks and 25 pressures against the Colts. Doing that again could hamper quarterback Deshaun Watson and the Browns, who have surrendered a league-high 24 sacks in six games. Cleveland left tackle Spencer Fano and right guard Austin Barber are both rookies. Titans eighth-year veteran Jeffery Simmons is arguably the NFL’s best defensive tackle. He has a team-high four sacks and 26 hurries. Where Cleveland Browns have edge vs. Titans Tennessee’s passing offense is the NFL’s worst at 153.5 yards per game, and the Browns rank eighth in passing defense at 205.2 yards per game. Pro Bowl cornerback Denzel Ward anchors a Cleveland secondary that ranks sixth in coverage grade at 71.1, according to Pro Football Focus. Cornerback Myles Harden has five passes defended this season. The Titans likely won’t win another game with a blocked punt return and four second-half field goals like they did against the Colts. If the Browns limit Cam Ward’s explosive plays downfield — they had six pass breakups against the Ravens — then Tennessee will struggle to score. Cam Ward has developed a go-to target in rookie receiver Carnell Tate, which is good. But receivers beyond Tate (44 targets) and Wan’Dale Robinson (37) aren’t that involved. Running back Tyjae Spears has more targets (17) than receiver Calvin Ridley (five). Elic Ayomanor has shown flashes of playmaking, but he’s averaging two targets the past four games and had a bad drop against the Colts. Score prediction: Browns 21, Titans 10 Ward’s limitations are clear through six games, giving Cleveland’s secondary a near-perfect blueprint. If nothing pops for Tennessee’s offense, the scoring woes will continue. Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? Reach him at tpalmateer@tennessean.com and on the X platform, @tpalmateer83 . away.headline: Is Quinshon Judkins playing today? Browns Week 6 injury report with RB banged up
away.blurb: Is Quinshon Judkins playing today? Browns RB1 a true game-time call After missing Cleveland's first two practices this week, Judkins returned as a limited participant on Friday, giving some hope that he might be able to push through his ankle issue against Baltimore. But on Sunday morning, Ian Rapoport poured some cold water on that optimism: It sounds like Judkins is a true game-time decision, with pregame workouts determining whether he'll be able to go. Dylan Sampson has already been ruled out for Week 6 as he ramps up after starting the season on injured reserve, and Raheim Sanders just got put on IR himself earlier in the week. The Browns picked up Audric Estime off the Vikings' practice squad, but as things stand, he and Jaleel McLaughlin are the only two running backs we can say with certainty will enter Sunday's game at something close to full health. Of the other two available options, McLaughlin would seem to be the preferable play from a fantasy perspective. He's more of a receiving back than the bruising Estime, but he's also been with the Browns all season, whereas Estime is just now getting up to speed with a new team. He's rarely shouldered double-digit carries at the NFL level, but he flashed some real versatility across three seasons with the Broncos before coming to Cleveland in 2026. Of course, if you want to steer clear of this backfield entirely, that's more than understandable given the uncertainty and the tough matchup. Some other viable flex options include Dameon Pierce, who's filling in for the injured Saquon Barkley in a beleaguered Eagles backfield on Sunday, and iffier options like Bears RB Roschon Johnson (filling in for an injured Kyle Monangai) and Patriots RB Corey Kiner (with TreVeyon Henderson out). Is Caleb Williams playing today? Bears Week 6 injury as QB eyes return Sunday's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens is the biggest game the Cleveland Browns have had in recent memory, with a chance to move to 4-2 and assume first place in the AFC North if they can find a way to upset Lamar Jackson and Co. at home. But this is the Browns we're talking about, so of course the football gods have seen fit to completely decimate Cleveland's backfield. Bellcow Quinshon Judkins left last week's loss to the New York Jets with an ankle injury after posting 44 yards on 14 carries. It's hard to overstate his importance to a Browns running back group that has essentially nothing in the way of proven production behind him. But while he's doing everything he can to suit up in Week 6 and seems to be trending in the right direction, his status remains very much up in the air just hours before kickoff. The fact that Judkins was able to at least get a practice in this week is a good sign that his injury isn't overly serious, as is the fact that the Browns opted not to call up another running back from the practice squad on Friday. away.headline: Cleveland Browns Practice Report for Wednesday, October 21 Week 7
away.blurb: Safety Grant Delpit, who has been nicked up, and suffered a concussion in the Week 6 victory over the Baltimore Ravens, did not practice. His absence might actually be liking to continue in the sessions on Thursday, and again Friday, when the official injury report is revealed. In addition, defensive tackle Kalia Davis (quadriceps) did not take part in Wednesday’s practice, and he remains on the reserve/injured list with a designation to return. The clock is ticking, as his 21-day practice window was opened 15 days ago , so a decision is coming soon. Several Players Listed as Limited Participants Defensive end Derek Barnett (ankle), wide receiver Denzel Boston (foot), defensive tackle Maliek Collins (foot), wide receiver KC Concepcion (calf, quadriceps), offensive tackle Tytus Howard (knee), running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and running back Dylan Sampson (knee) were each listed as limited participants. Sampson also had his 21-day window opened last week. The Cleveland Browns completed their first official practice Wednesday ahead of the Week 7 road game against the Tennessee Titans, and first-year head coach Todd Monken listed a total of 16 players who are nursing one or two injuries each. The group was able to take part in Wednesday’s practice session in varying degrees. Six Players Unable to Practice on Wednesday When practice took part at the CrossCountry Mortgage campus in Berea, there were a total of six players who were unable to participate in the session. We already covered Delpit, above, and he is likely to be touch-and-go this week. our first practice participation report for Week 7 https://t.co/K7QUs3kE3p Defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), center/offensive guard Elgton Jenkins (knee), offensive guard Teven Jenkins (back) and linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) also did not participant. Hall has not played since the Week 4 victory on Thursday night over the Pittsburgh Steelers, missing the past two games. Elgton Jenkins was able to play in the Week 6 win over the Baltimore Ravens, while Teven Jenkins hasn’t played a game all season after suffering a back injury in the practice Wednesday ahead of the Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. That has been a wasted roster spot all season. Schwesinger hasn’t missed any time despite nagging injuries, and he had a season-high 13 tackles against the Ravens, including five of the solo variety, while recording a half of a stuff with one forced fumble. Quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back) and linebacker Justin Jefferson (hip) practiced in full Wednesday. Gabriel is in the same boat as Kalia Davis, with his 21-day practice window closing within a week . The team has been able to keep four quarterbacks as a result of this maneuvering, but it likely will come to a head soon. It could come with one of the young quarterbacks being moved before the NFL trade deadline, but that’s speculation.

away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Browns’ latest injury update raises concerns ahead of Titans matchup
away.blurb: The Cleveland Browns are missing several notable players from practice ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans . Camryn Justice of News 5 reported on six total players expected to be out for Wednesday practice: Delpit would be a big miss for the Browns, with one interception, one sack, and 25 combined tackles this year. Luckily for the Browns, they added depth at safety in the draft, and rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has started to emerge in recent weeks, with 24 tackles and just two receptions allowed this season. The Browns have some insurance at the position while Delpit works toward a return. Carson Schwesinger has been a defensive star for the Browns this season. Unfortunately, Schwesinger has been dealing with an ankle injury in recent weeks. The injury kept him out of practice most of last week ahead of the Ravens matchup, and he was limited in Friday's final practice. With Schwesinger missing Wednesday's practice, the Browns appear to be taking a similar approach this week. However, if his performance against the Ravens is any indication, Schwesinger should be available against the Titans. Grant Delpit is one of the Browns' key defensive players and was injured after being accidentally struck by teammate Derek Barnett during a tackle attempt on Ravens running back Derrick Henry. Delpit is listed as having a shoulder injury as well as a concussion. Delpit is the most uncertain name on the Browns' injury report, as he sustained the concussion during Sunday's matchup against Baltimore. The NFL's concussion protocol can be difficult to navigate, and his absence from Wednesday's practice raises questions about his availability this Sunday. Elgton Jenkins has anchored the Browns' offensive line at center this season and has been a bright spot for the position group. Jenkins was listed with a knee injury ahead of Wednesday's practice after playing every offensive snap against the Ravens in Week 6. While his absence is worth monitoring, Jenkins' ability to play through last week's matchup is encouraging. For now, the Browns will hope the injury remains a practice concern rather than one that affects his availability on Sunday. The Browns' injury report remains long, but it shows some encouraging signs compared to last week's report ahead of the Ravens matchup. Mason Graham and Quinshon Judkins, who both missed the Ravens game, returned to practice, with signs pointing to both potentially returning to action against the Titans. While Delpit's status is concerning, the team has some depth at safety to help offset a potential absence. Meanwhile, Schwesinger and Jenkins have shown they can play through injuries, giving Cleveland reason to be optimistic heading into Sunday's matchup. Against a tough Ravens front giving up the eighth-fewest fantasy points to running backs, he isn't more than a flex option or RB2 at best this week.

away.blurb: While Cleveland saw several key contributors fully clear their injury status following Friday’s session, four players have been ruled out and another four carry questionable designations heading into Sunday's division clash. Rookie receiver KC Concepcion fully cleared concussion protocol, joining Tylan Wallace, Carsen Ryan, Tytus Howard, Elgton Jenkins, and Grant Delpit as full-go for Sunday. away.headline: Colts' Injury Woes Continue as 16 Players Appear on Week 7 Report
away.source: Indianapolis Colts On SI on MSN
away.blurb: Eleven players did not practice, while five were limited. Three listings were for rest — Keenan Allen, Charvarius Ward Sr. and Jonathan Taylor — and defensive tackle Jerry Tillery was absent for personal reasons. Tight end Tyler Warren is the name I'm watching most closely. Warren did not practice Wednesday due to the groin injury suffered late last week, which already cost him Sunday's game against Tennessee. Matt Goncalves (ankle), Drew Ogletree (ankle) and Rigoberto Sanchez (right foot) also sat out, while Jalen Travis (foot) was limited. Wide receiver Anthony Gould missed practice with a concussion, while Ashton Dulin was limited with a hamstring injury. Rookie Bryce Boettcher missed Wednesday's practice with a groin injury, and Jaylon Carlies was limited as he continues recovering from the rib injury that has kept him out of the last two games. Austin Ajiake was also limited while undergoing a concussion evaluation. If Carlies cannot return, Indianapolis could have to lean even more heavily on rookie CJ Allen, while recently re-signed veteran Germaine Pratt may become an option. And with Boettcher now on the report, this group is running out of healthy bodies. Just when it seemed things couldn't get much worse for the Indianapolis Colts, Wednesday's injury report brought another headache. Sunday's embarrassing 26-20 loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans dropped Indianapolis to 2-4. A day later, owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon fired general manager Chris Ballard, ending his tenure in his 10th season. Now, with undefeated Minnesota waiting on Sunday, 16 players from the Colts' 53-man roster appeared on the first injury report of the week. That's almost a third of the roster, and this team is only six games into the season. That leaves 12 players dealing with actual injuries. For a team desperate to turn things around, it's a troubling list. The Injury Bug Keeps Coming Back Sanchez suffered his injury against Tennessee, prompting Indianapolis to add veteran punter Thomas Morstead to the practice squad. Linebacker Depth Is Becoming a Real Problem On defense, things aren't looking much better. Three Key Cornerbacks Miss Practice Then there's the cornerback room, where Sauce Gardner (calf), Justin Walley (knee) and Ward all missed practice. Ward's absence was rest-related, but Gardner is considered week-to-week after injuring his calf against Tennessee. Losing him for any length of time would be a massive blow to an already struggling secondary. The Colts are allowing 27.3 points per game, and facing a 5-0 Vikings team isn't exactly an ideal opportunity to navigate this many injuries. This injury bug always seems to find its way back to Indianapolis. With jobs on the line and the season slipping away, the Colts need that trend to stop quickly. 3 Colts May See Increased Workloads Moving Forward Week 7 Power Rankings: Indianapolis Plummets After Disastrous Week Colts Interim General Manager Makes First Moves in New Role 5 Colts Who Could Be Trad

away.headline: Vikings Initial Injury Report vs. Colts: Kevin O'Connell's squad is getting healthier, and it's a crucial week
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: It’s a fascinating matchup between the two teams. The Vikings are 5-0 with a lot of momentum coming out of the bye week. The real intrigue is how good the offense is going to be. Kyler Murray has been improving within the scheme, and they are going to be a group to watch. The Minnesota Vikings are officially coming off of their bye week, with a battered Indianapolis Colts team coming to town. The Minnesota Vikings are set to host the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday afternoon, marking the third home game at U.S. Bank Stadium. Meanwhile, the Colts are 2-4 and just fired their general manager, Chris Ballard. A fi re sale could soon be coming for the Colts, and the Vikings could take advantage . Both teams have a lot of injuries, and it could be impactful on Sunday. The first injury report set the stage for what that could look like. Vikings Wednesday injury report Jefferson and Addison are both practicing, which is great for the Vikings. If they are both back on Sunday, it would mark the 19th snap the two of them have been eligible to play with Kyler Murray as a trio. The hope is both Christian Darrisaw and T.J. Hockenson will be healed from their concussions for Sunday’s game. There are a lot of names on the injury report, and that could be huge for the Vikings. The biggest names on the list are both on offense: RB Jonathan Taylor and TE Tyler Warren. Missing both players would be massive in preventing the Colts from getting a win. away.headline: Colts key playmaker remains sidelined with injury
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. Unfortunately, his return to the field remains unknown. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. Related Articles Bears React to NFL Announcement for QB Caleb Williams Following His Return According to Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk, Colts second-year tight end Tyler Warren was still sidelined on Wednesday with a groin injury. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. It didn’t take Warren long to establish himself as one of the best up-and-coming tight ends in the league, either. As a rookie, Warren racked up 76 catches for 817 yards and four touchdowns. away.headline: The latest on Colts CB Sauce Gardner's injury status
away.blurb: He does not believe it’s that serious this season, although Indianapolis head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Gardner is week to week. A player with a week-to-week status is unlikely to play on Sunday. “It’s definitely not as bad as last year,” Gardner said. “I think I’m in a good spot, for sure.” Because it’s in the same calf, the MRI made it obvious to Gardner that he’s in a better spot. Gardner initially missed three games after suffering the injury last season, returned for 35 snaps in the penultimate game of the season before reinjuring the calf. “It’s in the same muscle, but it’s not the same exact spot,” Gardner said. “Looking at the MRI, the exact spot where it happened last year is like scarred over, it’s taken care of. It’s in a different spot, but it’s much milder.” There is always the possibility that a soft-tissue injury can linger. Gardner has started every game this season; veteran cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt played in his place last week. “I’m not really concerned,” Gardner said. “I trust our training staff here, and like I said, it’s not as bad as last year.” We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. home.headline: Vikings-Colts First Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they have seven starters who did not practice Wednesday due to injury. They include linebacker Bryce Boettcher, cornerback Sauce Gardner, right guard Matt Gonglaves, punter Rigoberto Sanchez, right tackle Jalen Travis, slot cornerback Justin Walley, and tight end Tyler Warren. Slot Cornerback Justin Walley's injury is new. Not much else is known at this point, but his not practicing and Sauce Gardner already likely out on Sunday could leave the Colts' struggling secondary pretty thin at cornerback. We'll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Friday. home.headline: Almost entirely good news on Vikings' first injury report of Week 7
home.blurb: Everyone on the Vikings’ active roster was at the team’s Wednesday practice. Only three players were deemed limited participants: WR Justin Jefferson (ankle), RT Brian O’Neill (knee), and CB James Pierre (foot). Typically, being a limited participant on Wednesday isn’t a major cause for concern. O’Neill and Jefferson were both questionable going into the Saints game but were able to play, which suggests they should be fine this week as well. Pierre, the Vikings’ No. 3 cornerback is a new addition to the injury report. Jefferson’s ankle might not quite be 100 percent yet, but it would be surprising if he missed this game after coming out of the Saints game without any issues. “It’s good,” Jefferson said on Wednesday. “Still taking it day by day and trying to get it feeling better and better every single day. Still wake up with those aches and pains like everybody does. But still being able to come out here, practice, get on my feet and run through it, it definitely feels good.” The Vikings are missing a couple key guys on injured reserve in Donovan Jackson and Josh Oliver, who are both likely out for the season. Outside of that, they seem to be getting healthy at a good time. After this week’s Colts game — which certainly can’t be overlooked — the schedule is going to get quite a bit more daunting, so they’ll need all of their guys available. As we’ve expected, dating back to the aftermath of the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints, a well-timed bye week helped bring some positive news on Minnesota’s first injury report of Week 7. Running back Jordan Mason (thumb), wide receiver Jordan Addison (hamstring), tight end T.J. Hockenson (concussion), and left tackle Christian Darrisaw (concussion) all missed the win in New Orleans. All four were full participants in Wednesday’s practice at TCO Performance Center, meaning they’ll play on Sunday against the Colts barring a setback. Also a full participant was rookie depth cornerback Chuck Demmings (hamstring), who has been sidelined since Week 3. The game will be Jeff Hafley's first divisional game of the year, and his team will spend four of the next six weeks playing within the division. The Dolphins are riding a 2026 opening winless streak, one of only two teams without a victory, and the only team that has yet to lead a single game. There is good news on the injury front , good news on the attendance front, and hopefully some good news on the scoreboard. The Jets have shown this year that they are not the same pushovers from years past, but they still represent the next and best chance for a Dolphins win. So what do you need to know about this game? After having an extra week to prepare, can the Dolphins notch their first win of the season? The Jets are coming off a Week 6 loss to the Patriots, while the Dolphins remain winless. The Jets' defense is good, but they are not the best Miami has faced this season. That bodes well for the offense, which has struggled throughout the year. Miami should be able to move the ball consistently on the ground with Ollie Gordon II. The Jets are giving up 123 yards per game on the ground this year. Miami is also expected to have its full WR unit for the first time since Week 2. The return of Caleb Douglas is important, but Malik Willis still has to be more decisive with the ball. away.headline: Dolphins Week 7 Injury Report: Kyle Louis Returns to Practice
away.blurb: Despite cornerback Reese Taylor once again not practicing due to his quad injury, there are several players who may be making their return in Week 7. There are several players who were limited on Wednesday, which includes long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), edge Robert Beal (hamstring), wide receiver Caleb Douglas (ankle), tight end Will Kacmarek (hamstring), and running back Jaylen Wright (foot). Among those players are the return of linebacker Kyle Louis and wide receiver Caleb Douglas. Both were injured within one week of each other, leading to long layoffs from playing. Douglas might be a bit more further along than Louis, as he has been out for a bit longer. Dolphins Week 7 Injury Report: Kyle Louis Returns to Practice - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Dolphins Week 7 Injury Report: Kyle Louis Returns to Practice (Kyle Terada-Imagn Images) James Brizuela Thu, October 22, 2026 at 2:25 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins have released their initial injury report, and the team has mostly good news. The full injurt report is as follows: Louis was pegged to be a strong starter, and he had impressed through training camp and preseason. He suffered a knee injury early on in Week 1 and has not played since. Douglas suffered an ankle injury in Week 2 and has since been attempting to make his way back to the field. Douglas was the top target for Malik Willis prior to the injury. With the chance that the rookie pass catcher returns on Sunday, that could be a big boost to the ailing offense. There were also several players who were full participants despite dealing with injuries. Cornerback Juju Brents (heel), linebacker Jordyn Brooks (foot), guard Jonah Savaiinaea (ankle), quarterback Malik Willis (right thumb), and linebacker Jackson Woodard (ankle). Savaiinaea suffered an ankle injury in Week 5 and exited the game. This led to Jarrett Kingston taking over. Savaiinaea returning to practice and being a full participant is good news for the Dolphins offense and the offensive line. Willis also did not throw during the team's practice session during the bye week, but head coach Jeff Hafley had indicated that his absence from throwing was nothing. That appears to be the case, as the quarterback was a full participant on Wednesday. Getting both Douglas and Louis back will be big, but it all depends on how they respond to ramping back up to football activities. Hafley stated that both would be tested on Wednesday and throughout the week to determine if they can play. Either way, the Dolphins have a strong chance to have most of their starters back for this important Week 7 divisional game.

away.headline: Miami Dolphins Stock Report: Rest Helps, but Proof Must Come Sunday
away.blurb: Caleb Douglas: Up, health permitting. Douglas returned to limited work Monday after an ankle injury. His size and speed could diversify a receiving group that has generated only two passing touchdowns. His stock depends on completing the practice week without a setback. Miami Dolphins Stock Report: Rest Helps, but Proof Must Come Sunday - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Miami Dolphins Stock Report: Rest Helps, but Proof Must Come Sunday Mark H. Stowers Wed, October 21, 2026 at 8:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Miami's overall stock remains down at 0-5, but the Dolphins enter Jets week with a healthier roster, a productive running game and two weeks to correct the mistakes that defined their first five losses. Team stock: Holding near the bottom. The Dolphins rank 31st in scoring at 14 points per game, 28th in total offense and last in sacks with four. They also carry a minus-4 turnover differential. The bye created preparation time, not proof of improvement. Miami's stock cannot rise meaningfully until it leads and wins. Ollie Gordon II: Up. Gordon has become the offense's most dependable player. The rookie leads Miami with 236 rushing yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5 yards per carry. He has produced 188 yards and two scores in his past two starts. New England's 148 rushing yards against the Jets reinforced Miami's reason to feature him. Kevin Coleman Jr.: Up. Coleman caught his first NFL touchdown against Cincinnati and received seven targets. Miami's passing game needs another receiver to emerge beside Malik Washington. Coleman's role should grow after the bye. Jarrett Kingston: Up. Kingston played well after Jonah Savaiinaea injured his ankle against Cincinnati. Whether he starts or returns to reserve duty, he gives Miami credible interior depth against New York's pressure packages. Malik Willis: Down. Willis is expected to play after a minor undisclosed issue, but his three turnovers against Cincinnati remain the central concern. His 849 passing yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions leave Miami vulnerable whenever the game shifts away from the run. Pass rush: Down. Zach Sieler leads Miami with two sacks, and the team has only four. Geno Smith has been sacked 19 times, creating an opportunity, but the Dolphins must show they can finish pressures. Special teams: Down until corrected. Cincinnati returned the opening kickoff 81 yards and Miami later missed an extra point. A low-scoring divisional game leaves little room for similar errors. The bye improved several health and preparation trends. Sunday determines whether that progress is real. Gordon, Coleman and the interior line are rising. Willis, the pass rush and special teams must reverse their direction for Miami to earn its first victory.

away.headline: Dolphins-Jets injury report: Hall sits, Miami waits for full practice data
away.blurb: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said running back Breece Hall would not practice Wednesday because of a quadriceps injury, although Hall had not been ruled out for Sunday. Braelon Allen has led New York with 314 rushing yards on 74 carries and would remain the primary back if Hall cannot play. Receiver Adonai Mitchell was expected to practice on a limited basis because of a finger injury. Left guard Dylan Parham is dealing with a knee injury. Edge rusher Joseph Ossai has an ankle problem, linebacker Kiko Mauigoa has a leg issue and slot corner Jarvis Brownlee Jr. has been monitored in the concussion process. Tight end Mason Taylor also appears on the Jets’ broader injury watch with a thumb issue. Miami’s most important offensive injury involves Jonah Savaiinaea . The starting right guard returned to limited work Monday after injuring his ankle against Cincinnati. Jarrett Kingston played well in relief and is the likely replacement if Savaiinaea cannot handle a full workload. Receiver Caleb Douglas also returned on a limited basis Monday after missing time with an ankle injury. His availability would add size and speed to a group led by Malik Washington, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr. Cornerback JuJu Brents is recovering from a neck injury or stinger, safety Michael Taaffe has a chest concern, cornerback Reese Taylor has dealt with a quadriceps injury and edge rusher Robert Beal Jr. has been limited by a hamstring problem. Tight end Justin Joly remains a concussion question. Quarterback Malik Willis is expected to play after tending to a minor undisclosed issue coming out of the Cincinnati game. Miami also may receive help from players eligible to return from reserve lists, including cornerbacks Storm Duck and Darrell Baker Jr. and edge defender Trey Moore. Eligibility does not guarantee activation, but those decisions could address thin positions. Wednesday participation is only the first checkpoint. Thursday will show whether limited players progress, and Friday will provide the official game designations. The first complete Dolphins-Jets injury picture remained in development Wednesday, but several key players entered the practice week with uncertain availability. Miami must monitor its right guard, secondary and receiving depth, while New York’s backfield and offensive line remain the major questions. The matchup effects are direct. Savaiinaea’s status influences protection against a 17-sack defense. Brents and the other corners affect Miami’s ability to cover Wilson and Cooper. Hall’s availability changes New York’s backfield rotation, while Parham’s knee could weaken the Jets’ protection against a Dolphins pass rush desperate for production.

away.headline: Dolphins QB Malik Willis practices fully despite thumb injury
away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: "Sometimes it's nine out of 11, 10 out of 11 doing the right thing and one person is not, and it'll mess up the whole play," Willis said. "It's not always that evident watching from the outside, but when we get into the film room, 'Okay, that's what we mean when we're like, it's that close.' You know what I mean? It's easy to say. But you guys go by the results and we haven't been proven those." MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis was treated for an injured thumb on his right, throwing hand, but fully practiced four days before a Week 7 game at the New York Jets. Willis did not throw at a bye week Monday practice that was open to reporters. Willis did not mention the thumb injury when he met with reporters a short time before the first Jets injury report of the week was released. "(Coach Jeff Hafley) just wanted to get us a little rest, and he wanted to get some young guys in there and see how they were progressing through this season," Willis said when asked what he was dealing with. But, pretty good." Hafley said at the start of the week that Willis would be fine. "He should be good," Hafley said. "I mean, was he dealing with something? Yeah, I mean, we had a bunch of guys after the game that were and having a Tuesday practice, usually we don't go until Wednesday. So just rested him on that, but I foresee him being good to go." Miami Dolphins injury report includes Malik Willis thumb Willis has said he hasn't been good enough in his first five Dolphins starts. WIllis is 29th in the NFL with a passer rating of 68.4. He's got 2 passing touchdowns, 2 rushing touchdowns, 4 interceptions and 5 fumbles. Willis said he balanced football review and rest and recovery during the bye week. What does Willis think about outside of football? "I mean, the Lord, bro," Willis said. "I keep waking up every day. I got an opportunity to come in here and do my job. I have a family that loves me. I have more than enough. I make it to work safe every day, bro. It's a dangerous world. And we just overlook all these things that are blessings. I try not to do that. And at the same time, I hold myself to the highest of standards. And I just try to focus on the process. Am I doing anything in my power? If I make sure the process is right, the results will come." home.blurb: The Jets injury report for October 21 features Breece Hall sitting out Wednesday’s practice, while Adonai Mitchell and Dylan Parham participated on a limited basis as New York prepares to host the Miami Dolphins. Mitchell’s limited participation gives the Jets another situation to watch as the week unfolds. Asked whether the receiver’s availability would come down to pain tolerance, Glenn confirmed that was a factor. The coach sounded more optimistic about T’Vondre Sweat and Will McDonald. Both were limited, but Glenn said he expected each to be fine. Their participation over the next two days will provide a clearer picture. Glenn also discussed Omar Cooper Jr.’s return from injured reserve and the additional dimension he brings to the passing game. The coach highlighted Cooper’s deep-ball ability alongside his work after the catch. With Mitchell still working back and Hall’s status unsettled, having Cooper available gives the Jets another offensive weapon as they prepare for Miami. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing Aaron Glenn left the door open for Hall to progress during the week. The Jets running back is dealing with a quad injury, but Wednesday’s absence does not establish his availability for Sunday. “He won’t practice today, and we’ll see how tomorrow operates to see how he goes during the week,” Glenn said. Glenn praised Hall’s approach to his recovery, saying he has attacked the process with the same intensity he brings to preparing for a game. Getting him back on the practice field would be an encouraging next step, but that remains something to monitor. Wednesday’s participation and injury designations come from the Jets official report . No game statuses have been assigned yet. Adonai Mitchell Working Back, Sunday Still Uncertain “Yeah, I would say that. His progress bears watching as the Jets look to get healthier on offense heading into a division matchup. Mauigoa and Ossai Remain Week-to-Week Glenn described Kiko Mauigoa and Joseph Ossai as week-to-week. Both missed Wednesday’s practice, along with running back Kene Nwangwu. Omar Cooper Jr. Gives the Offense a Lift “I don’t want to say that it surprised me, but it was just good to see that we have another weapon back and doing the things that we expect him to do,” Glenn said. Thursday’s practice should offer the next meaningful update, particularly on Hall and whether Mitchell can increase his workload. home.headline: Aaron Glenn's conflicting injury updates raise new questions for Jets
home.blurb: "I think he waited like a week, week and a half before he had to see how he actually was going to progress and then we wanted to go ahead and get it knocked out," Glenn said. There is good news on the injury front, though. Rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. had his practice window open and was a limited participant in New York's walkthrough. The Indiana product being back on the field is huge for their offense. "He's a really good player, but you never want any rookie to actually miss time because the reps are valuable for these guys," Glenn said. "And I think all of our rookies that's been getting these reps have been valuable, and we have a number of guys that's been out of practice." Why Omar Cooper Jr.'s Return Is Even More Crucial for the Jets' 2026 Outlook Gamesmanship knows no bounds in the modern NFL. Coaches will try to conceal the severity of injuries for as long as they possibly can in order to get a small advantage over their opponents, even if it means confusing their fanbase for weeks. That's what has happened to the New York Jets in their latest injury report. Head coach Aaron Glenn has always been coy on injuries. This week, though, he went back on previous comments made just last week. When it comes to wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, the former second-round pick has missed the last three weeks due to a finger injury. Glenn provided this update on the wideout last week: "He's progressing faster than we thought that he would," Glenn said last Friday. "Once we got to the end of it of knowing exactly what the prognosis was when it comes to his finger." When asked outright if Mitchell received a procedure during his time off, Glenn was adamant: Wednesday, Glenn provided a different update, and it leaves more questions than answers. Glenn confirmed to reporters on Wednesday that Mitchell did in fact have a procedure done early into the recovery on his finger. The lack of transparency is nothing new. Glenn is not doing anything different than 31 other coaches around the league do. At the same time, it does open questions about other injured players that the team is dealing with. More Jets injuries cloud the Week 6 outlook Running back Breece Hall, edge rusher Joseph Ossai, and left guard Dylan Parham are all week to week. Ossai has been going back and forth on the field with a foot injury that has been bothering him since training camp. But can Jets fans trust he'll actually have a chance to play in the next few weeks? Remember, the ankle injury suffered has kept him off the field for four of the first five games of his NFL career. Those are valuable reps, both in practice and in games, that Cooper has missed. Expecting him to walk into Week 6 and be able to be productive isn't fair to the player. But it also adds additional questions. If Cooper's practice window is open, that positions the Jets to open up a short-term IR slot. Will someone take his place? home.headline: New York Jets Hope to See Return of Breece Hall for Miami Dolphins Game
home.blurb: Jets running back Breece Hall has teased on social media that he could return from a quad injury for the 2-4 team’s game against the winless Miami Dolphins this weekend. In other news, the long-lost Adonai Mitchell is expected to return to practice today on a limited basis. Mitchell injured his finger when he caught it in the jersey of a teammate during practice. He was off to a good start in his season, firmly establishing his credentials as the No. 2 receiver. There was a question on what kind of injury he had, and head coach Aaron Glenn finally had to admit that Mitchell underwent some sort of “procedure” on his injured digits. When he will be a full-go to return is still up in the air, and the team is now saying pain tolerance will be a factor. Mitchell has nine catches for 123 yards in two games. In his Wednesday address to the media, head coach Glenn said that Hall’s return wouldn’t disrupt the backfield flow. In new injury news, defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat and edge rusher Will McDonald were listed as limited on the injury report. Running back/kick returner Kene Nwangwu, who took some punishing hits on the return squad in the New England game, will sit out practices for now Help is on the way for the New York Jets, who have been missing some key players on offense. A quadriceps injury is damage to the four muscles or tendon on the front of the thigh, commonly caused by a muscle strain, direct bruise (contusion), or tendon tear. Symptoms include sudden sharp pain, swelling, bruising, and trouble straightening the knee. All are key attributes for an NFL running back. Hall sustained the injury at the end of the Detroit Lions game in Week 3. At the time, it wasn’t considered major, but he’s since missed three games. In his stead, backup Braelon Allen has been a tremendous replacement, and could share time in the backfield with Hall. However, his injury proved to be a bit of a Jets conundrum. Mitchell has missed the last four games and was not placed on injured reserve, thus taking up a roster spot that could have been put to better use. Also on the mend is left guard Dylan Parham, who has now missed three games with a knee injury. Parham was a steadying presence on the left side of the line, and had high PFF scores during his playing time. “Breece is our starter, he’s always been our starter,” Glenn said. “But, as always, Braelon’s going to get his touches, too.” Glenn added that edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) and linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (thigh) will be week to week. It’s likely neither will play against Miami.

away.blurb: The Buccaneers are running out of time to turn their season around. Entering Week 7, the team is 1-5, and if they want to make it back into the playoffs they need to start winning games. Unfortunately, Irving landed on the injury report for Wednesday’s practice. Irving was listed as a DNP due to an illness that is going around the locker room. Tampa Bay’s practice report on Wednesday was telling for a few reasons as some important names popped up. The Buccaneers were also without their backup running back in Week 6, as Sean Tucker did not play due to a quad injury against the Minnesota Vikings, leaving Tampa Bay to rely almost solely on Bucky Irving. Irving is having an excellent third NFL season. He has rushed for 452 yards on 96 attempts. He was not the only skill position player to land on the report, with Emeka Egbuka also missing practice due to both a concussion and a foot injury. home.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles revealed that he'll make a decision regarding quarterback Baker Mayfield's availability on Friday ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Carolina Panthers, per ESPN's Jenna Laine . Mayfield has missed each of Tampa Bay's past three games due to a dislocated right thumb that he suffered during a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, but returned to practice on Wednesday. Bowles explained that Mayfield threw the ball well during Wednesday's session and did well in what he was asked to do, per Laine. If the signal-caller isn't able to suit up against Carolina, the Buccaneers will stick with Jalon Daniels under center. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

home.headline: Baker Mayfield Injury Update Doesn't Improve Buccaneers' Odds vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7
home.blurb: On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was unable to do enough to get the Bucs a second win in a row, and the team is in last place in the NFC South entering Week 7. That would be a major boost to a Tampa Bay team that needs a winning streak to get back in the mix to make the playoffs. Despite the report from Pelissero, oddsmakers aren't buying the Bucs on the road against the first-place Panthers and Bryce Young. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves.
