Chase Brown won't be completely forgotten; he is still more explosive than Brown. But Perine could easily take the lion's share of a 55/45 split. He is better between the tackles, and it's time for the Bengals to capitalize on their stellar run-blocking and get closer to the league average, as they currently rank 28th in the NFL with 82.8 rushing yards per game. Rumors are swirling that the Bengals could target Jonathan Taylor or Tony Pollard in the trade market. I'd expect them to see what they have with Perine as the #1 option over the next few weeks before deciding. Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase makes 12 catches for over 125 yards Chase has been disappointing this season, at least in terms of production. He's still had moments that cement him as the NFL's best wide receiver, like his stellar catches against the Houston Texans and Miami Dolphins. He hasn't eclipsed 100 yards this season, and yes, that number is basically semantics when you see he had 98 yards in Cincinnati's loss to the Steelers. He hasn't gone more than five games without 100+ yards in a single season since his rookie year, when he went from October 31 to December 19, seven games, without reaching triple digits in receiving yards. It's only a matter of time before he breaks out and has a stellar game like he's capable of. Baltimore's pass defense is about league average, and Chase averages just over 120 yards against the Ravens in his career. Expect him to hit a couple big plays to put him over the hump. Right tackle Amarius Mims doesn't allow a pressure facing Trey Hendrickson Mims has been great this season, allowing only four pressures in five games. Through the first four weeks, Mims allowed just two pressures despite facing talented edge rushers like Rueben Bain Jr., Will Anderson, and TJ Watt. He will have extra motivation going against his former teammate, Trey Hendrickson. Reports suggest the Bengals locker room wasn't too fond of Hendrickson during his time with the franchise, so Mims will have every reason to bring his absolute best against him in a game that could push the Bengals into first place in the division.

Sunday afternoon, the Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) and the Baltimore Ravens (4-2) meet at M&T Bank Stadium meet with each looking to take the next chapter in this rivalry and in the process take possession of the top spot in the division. The Bengals have not played since October 11 against the Dolphins. Cincy won 31-24. Cincinnati’s offense looked much more like the explosive unit that has defined the Joe Burrow era, generating points consistently against a Miami defense that struggled to contain the Bengals’ passing attack. The victory snapped a two-game losing streak and improved Cincinnati’s record to 3-2 heading into its Week 6 bye last weekend. The extra week of rest could prove valuable as the Bengals prepare for a Baltimore defense that has traditionally made life difficult on divisional opponents. Baltimore sits tied atop the division with Cleveland and Pittsburgh because they lost last weekend to the aforementioned Browns, 13-10. Quarterback Lamar Jackson did not play in the game and the offense labored without him. The Ravens entered that game having won three of four and had averaged more than 29 points per game before being held to just 10 by the Browns. Jackson is listed as day-to-day with continued ankle issues. Several compelling storylines will define this matchup. Baltimore’s elite rushing attack, led by Derrick Henry’s 534 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, faces a Cincinnati defense that ranks among the league’s better units against the run. On the other side, Burrow will look to exploit a Ravens’ secondary that has occasionally surrendered big plays through the air. The recent rivalry has also produced some memorable games, with the teams splitting their 2025 meetings and several contests in recent years being decided by one possession. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two in this AFC North tilt. picks.headline: Bengals vs. Ravens bold predictions for AFC North clash in Week 7
picks.blurb: For the Cincinnati Bengals , Ja’Marr Chase saved some money by appealing. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That’s because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens’ defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they’ve been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. “The turnovers is what screams at you,” Taylor said. “That leads into field position.” And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. “It’s exciting,” Taylor said. “I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don’t get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it’s a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it.” Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. “I think we’ll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out,” Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. “Every game’s different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact.” The Bengals haven’t forgotten about their ground game. “You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass,” Pitcher said. “You’re always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It’s like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we’re getting in a game on a given Sunday.” Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week’s fumble that led to the Ravens’ loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. “I got to take care of the ball,” he said. “There’s no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm’s way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can’t put the team in that situation.” Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. “Obviously, he’s Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball,” Hamilton said. “He knows that. He’s his harshest critic, so I’m not going to say anything ill about it. He’s put us in position to win a lot of games.” All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he’s back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he’s back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. away.headline: Concerning Lamar Jackson Injury Update Shifts Bengals vs. Ravens Odds in NFL Week 7
away.blurb: Concerning Lamar Jackson Injury Update Shifts Bengals vs. Ravens Odds in NFL Week 7 Skip to main content ON SI Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has not played since Week 4, and his status for Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals still remains unclear. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson could "potentially" practice this week after missing all three of the team's practices ahead of Week 6. There have been reports the last two weeks that Jackson has a chance to play through his ankle injury, but he has not suited up in practice -- or for a game -- since Week 4. Minter: Lamar Jackson (ankle) could "potentially" practice this week. Remains day-to-day. Minter's update on Jackson isn't viewed as a positive one in the betting market. Ahead of Week 7, oddsmakers set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Bengals. Now, DraftKings Sportsbook has Baltimore set as a 2.5-point favorite, though it remains -148 on the moneyline to win this game. It's not a major adjustment, but clearly there is some worry that Jackson could miss his third game in a row. Currently, DraftKings has received 73 percent of the moneyline bets in this game on the Bengals to win outright. After going down against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, Jackson has not played. He missed a win over Atlanta in Week 5 and a loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. The Cleveland loss looms large for the Ravens, as they are now behind the Browns in the AFC North standings. The Ravens are a much more dangerous team with Jackson in the lineup, and he was an MVP candidate before going down in Week 4. This season, the star quarterback has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. A two-time MVP, Jackson leads the league in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating in 2026. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score, a sign that his rushing is back to a higher level than it was in 2025. Tyler Huntley would receive the start in Week 7 if Jackson can't go. Dating back to last season, the Ravens are 3-1 in Huntley's last four starts, but they remain 7-12 all-time when Jackson is sidelined. Huntley struggled to move the offense in Week 6, throwing for 165 yards and a score in a 13-10 loss. He did combine for three scores in the win over Atlanta, so there is a higher ceiling that what he showed this past Sunday. If Jackson doesn't practice on Wednesday, it's possible this line could move even further towards the Bengals. For now, oddsmakers are still giving the Ravens the edge in this divisional battle. away.headline: Bengals injury report: secondary piece working back to field, Lamar Jackson's latest status revealed
away.blurb: The Bengals checked one practice box during Ravens week and came out pretty clean on the Wednesday injury report. Cincinnati had a couple of veterans go limited due to rest and reacclimation this week, but Kyle Dugger (quad) was the only active player who didn't practice on Wednesday. On the Ravens side, Lamar Jackson (ankle) was a limited player on Wednesday in his first practice since suffering the injury in Week 4. Check out the full statuses below: Cincinnati has another practice on Thursday afternoon. Check out the full report from both teams, including a lot of banged-up names for Baltimore: The Bengals and Ravens are the top two favorites to win the AFC North, and Sunday's winner gets a big leg up in the race. They don't play again until the New Year's Eve battle in Cincinnati. "The divisional game is always big, so I think that's our focus right now," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said on Monday. "It's just go on the road, tremendous opportunity to go on the road versus a great team, find a way to get a win, and put yourself in a good position. "If we don't focus on the details all week, then none of that's going to matter. So I think these guys-they understand that. We've said that over and over again. But I am excited to go on the road. Tremendous opportunity right in front of us. Again, I think when two great teams play each other, it always makes for a fun game. And so look forward to the week of prep and see how we end up on Sunday." Cincinnati should have its healthiest group of players since Week 1 if no other setbacks or new injuries pop up in the next few days. Bryan Cook is one of a few impact players who's gotten much healthier across the bye and early part of Week 7. "Yeah, I think he feels a lot better now," Taylor said about Cook. "Coming off the bye week, moving around today, watching him move around, I think the confidence of being closer to 100% I hate to put a percentage on him, but I think he feels a lot better than he probably did two weeks ago, three weeks ago, and so it's good to get him back closer to full strength." away.headline: Ravens list 15 players on Wednesday injury report ahead of Bengals
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Lamar Jackson was listed as limited Wednesday with an ankle injury, while Cam Jurgens was a full participant as he continued working toward his Baltimore debut. Outside linebacker Tavius Robinson did not participate because of a pectoral injury. Jackson’s designation was the biggest update after he missed the opening portion of practice available to reporters. Coach Jesse Minter later said Jackson got limited work, and the official report confirmed his participation. Rashod Bateman was listed as limited with a shoulder injury after exiting Sunday’s loss to Cleveland. Bateman has 16 receptions for 233 yards and a touchdown, with 11 catches producing first downs. Rookie tight end Matthew Hibner also was listed as limited with a hand injury. Hibner has five catches for 70 yards and a touchdown. Cornerback T.J. Tampa, designated for return from injured reserve, was listed as limited with rest, toe, and ankle designations. He recorded 29 tackles, two passes defensed and an interception last season. Calais Campbell joined Robinson as the only nonparticipants, receiving a rest day. Mark Andrews and Trey Hendrickson practiced fully despite hand and finger injuries, respectively. Baltimore listed 15 players overall. Thursday’s practice will provide the next indication of whether Wednesday’s progress carries into the remainder of Bengals week. Tampa remains on injured reserve and has been designated for return. The Ravens’ first official injury report ahead of Sunday’s matchup against Cincinnati brought encouraging developments at quarterback and center, along with a new concern for their defensive front. Jackson has missed two consecutive games after leaving the Tennessee matchup at halftime on Oct. 4. In four appearances, he has completed 68 of 96 passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, posting a 119.6 passer rating. He also has 144 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Jurgens practiced without a red non-contact jersey and was listed as a full participant with a concussion. Full participation is encouraging, though it does not independently confirm completion of concussion protocol or availability against Cincinnati. Before the trade from Philadelphia, Jurgens played 242 offensive snaps this season, including 187 at left guard and 55 at center. Pro Football Focus charged him with 12 pressures allowed, including one sack, across 146 pass-blocking snaps. away.headline: Colbie Young injury update more good news for Bengals
away.blurb: Young was due for just that earlier this season while other wideouts were injured, only to suffer an injury of his own that’s held him out. After encouraging signs before the bye week, Young sounds ready for a full-blown comeback, based on commentary from Bengals head coach Zac Taylor. "He's looked as good as he's looked in a long time," Taylor said . "I think last week he had a good week on what he could handle from a rehab perspective. So this week to get him back involved, he looked good running around today. I think it's good to finally get him back and feel like he's closer to 100% healthy." This is a key one for the Bengals and Young. For the rookie, he has a chance to prove those hyped summer flashes were the real deal. And for Joe Burrow’s offense, it’s still missing third wideout Andrei Iosivas and situational tight end Tanner Hudson. Young’s big enough and talented enough to help fill that void. home.headline: Lamar Jackson injury takes concerning turn ahead of Ravens' crucial Bengals clash
home.blurb: A divisional loss at home with the backup under centre would widen a hole the Ravens are already in, and Jackson’s own level of urgency has not been in question inside the building. Minter said on Monday that his quarterback had been working his tail off to get back and had stayed on top of Huntley’s preparation during his time out. Help from the trade market is not likely to arrive at quarterback, or anywhere else expensive. General manager Eric DeCosta has roughly $2.16 million in available salary cap space, the third-lowest total in the NFL, as the Ravens’ own in-house mailbag laid out on Tuesday. Lamar Jackson was not on the field when the Baltimore Ravens opened their Week 7 preparation on Wednesday. He was listed as a non-participant on the team’s first injury report of the week, extending his absence from training since he sprained his ankle in the Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans on October 4. Head coach Jesse Minter, in his first year after replacing John Harbaugh in January , had left the door open earlier in the week. On Monday he classified Jackson as day-to-day and said he could potentially practice at some point. “I’d still put it in kind of the day-to-day thing,” Minter told reporters . “We’ll know a lot more on Wednesday, I would say.” Wednesday did not deliver the clarity Baltimore was looking for. Read also: Sergio Perez claims Formula 1 rule is doing the exact opposite of what it was designed for Backup Tyler Huntley has run the offence in each of the last two games, splitting the two. Baltimore edged the Atlanta Falcons 30-23 in overtime before falling 13-10 at home to the Cleveland Browns last Sunday. Against the Browns, Huntley completed 19 of 31 passes for 165 yards and a touchdown , and the Ravens scored no points after the first quarter. Jackson’s own numbers before the injury were MVP-level. Through four games he had passed for 967 yards with six touchdowns and one interception at a 70.8% completion rate, and he had added 144 rushing yards and a score. Divisional stakes at M&T Bank Stadium Kickoff at M&T Bank Stadium is at 1pm local time on Sunday. The game will be carried nationally on CBS , with Paramount+ streaming it locally. On October 7 the Ravens acquired Pro Bowl centre Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick, with the Ravens also receiving a 2027 seventh-rounder. Baltimore had been down to its fourth centre of the season after injuries up front, and any further additions before the November 4 deadline are expected to be modest. The next formal update on Jackson’s status will come when the Ravens release their Thursday injury report, with a final game designation to follow on Friday. picks.blurb: Week 6 was a tough one for the Giants . Despite a double digit lead in the first half, the Giants (3-2-1) surrendered a whopping 34 unanswered points in a 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints (2-4) at MetLife Stadium. With quarterback Jameis Winston benched, the G-Men fought back with recently acquired QB J.J. McCarthy shining during his debut in the fourth quarter, with the former No. 10 overall pick putting up 243 passing yards and a touchdown in only 11 minutes under center. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. The biggest question now will be is it McCarthy or Winston under center in Week 7? Regardless of which QB it is, it'll be a tough task for either signal caller when the Giants head to Houston to face the surging Texans (2-4) this Sunday afternoon. Our NFL prognosticators are: Art Stapleton ( Giants /NFL writer, NorthJersey.com), Bert Bainbridge (sports trending reporter/columnist, NorthJersey.com), Brian Marron (digital producer, NorthJersey.com), Chris Iseman (Rutgers writer, NorthJersey.com), Mike Dougherty (sports writer, lohud.com), Bob Jordan (sports editor, Asbury Park Press/APP.com) and Dave Rivera (sports editor, USA TODAY Northeast/NorthJersey.com). Will J.J. McCarthy’s impressive performance in relief of Jameis Winston be enough to unseat him as the starter? If the Giants can’t run the football, this entire team’s philosophy in having all three phases work together might be a house of cards. There remains an opportunity in the division, but it's alarming how the bottom has fallen out of run game. Personnel? Execution? Scoreboard? Yes. John Harbaugh and his coaching staff are in for a long week with plenty of fixes and a good start to this season at stake. Big Blue stays keeps it within reach, but never close enough as Houston takes the one by two touchdowns. McCarthy this week's starter at quarterback speaks volumes. The pick: Texans 23, Giants 16 Here's why: Inconsistency is causing the Giants to decline a bit lately, and it's bad timing to be making this trip to face a Texans team that is showing signs of improvement. The pick: Texans 31, Giants 17 Here's why: These Giants are hard to predict, but their loss to the Saints showed they could be coming back to reality. With the quarterback situation, they're not a very good team right now. Mike Dougherty The pick: Texans 28, Giants 20 Here's why: A feel-good start masked the problems that are now surfacing. It's pretty clear after last week, the Giants are exactly what most believed they would be this season, a work in progress. The pick: Texans 34, Giants 17 Here's why: The Texans are surging thanks to C.J. Stroud quietly playing some of the best football of any QB in the NFL. Houston's defense is not as strong as last season, but the Giants have major questions on offense with the starting quarterback and main option at running back still in flux. picks.headline: 3 J.J. McCarthy bold predictions for first start with Giants in Week 7 vs. Texans
picks.blurb: The New York Giants have already had quite the up and down season through six games. New York is 3-2-1 on the season after losing Jaxon Dart for the season in addition to a platoon of defensive injuries. Fortunately, the Giants have been able to stay alive and keep their playoff hopes intact as they approach the middle of the season. The next twist of the season will come in Week 7 after J.J. McCarthy was named the starter on Wednesday. McCarthy took over for Jameis Winston during the fourth quarter in Week 6 and moved the offense surprisingly well. Now the Giants will give him a full audition against the Texans this weekend. Will this experiment work out well for Big Blue? Or will McCarthy crash and burn just like he did in Minnesota? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Here are three bold predictions ahead of McCarthy’s first start in New York against a scary Houston defense. McCarthy will throw for fewer passing yards than he had in Week 6 McCarthy only played the final 11 and a half minutes of the fourth quarter against the Saints. But he certainly made the most of that time. The young quarterback ended that game going 11-of-21 for 243 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception. That is a huge volume of throws to make in one quarter. In fact, that stat line would be solid enough for an entire game’s output given McCarthy’s track record. At this point, it would be foolish to assume that McCarthy can replicate that performance on a consistent basis. But it is fascinating to consider how well McCarthy could spin it if he gets into a rhythm for a whole game. Still, Giants fans should rein in their optimism until McCarthy plays a complete 60 minutes of good football. McCarthy will fail to eclipse 243 passing yards in Week 7 against an elite Texans defense. But realistically, the quality of McCarthy’s play should mean more than his raw accounting stats. McCarthy will force feed targets to Malik Nabers It will be interesting to see what kind of game plan the Giants cook up for McCarthy. He has similar skills to Dart, but fully installing the Dart offense could be a big ask ahead of Week 7. Nabers and Isaiah Likely were two of McCarthy’s favorite targets against the Saints. Once McCarthy entered the game, Nabers logged four catches for 95 yards on five targets. That volume could go through the roof in a larger sample size. Especially considering the woeful state of New York’s rushing attack, with or without Cam Skattebo . McCarthy will target Nabers at least 20 times against the Texans on Sunday. Houston’s defense will throttle McCarthy, forcing multiple sacks and turnovers Houston’s defense has not consistently played elite ball this season. However, the Texans still have that incredibly high gear when their defense is firing on all cylinders. Even in a reduced state, McCarthy should be worried about DeMeco Ryans’ defense . The Texans have 18 sacks through six games , which is tied for third in the NFL with the Broncos. They haven’t been as successful at forcing turnovers, with only six on the season. That could change against the Giants if some of McCarthy’s bad habits pop up while he’s under pressure. The Texans will sack McCarthy at least four times in Week 7. Beyond that, they will force the young quarterback to commit at least two turnovers. For maximum boldness, that will be at least one interception with a lost fumble on a sack. This one could get ugly, Giants fans. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. picks.headline: Giants’ John Harbaugh makes J.J. McCarthy vs. Jameis Winston pick for Week 7 vs. Texans
picks.blurb: The New York Giants will be facing the Houston Texans in Week 7, and many have been wondering who the starting quarterback will be. J.J. McCarthy came into the game last week during the second half and almost led the team to victory, and that may have been enough for head coach John Harbaugh to give him the start. It was indeed enough, as McCarthy is set to be QB1 , according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. “Source: The Giants plan to start J.J. McCarthy on Sunday vs. Houston,” Fowler wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It felt like a no-brainer for the Giants, especially with how Jameis Winston had played over the past few weeks. Yes, he led them to some wins, but the last two weeks were not great. Against the Washington Commanders, they ended the game in a tie, and against the New Orleans Saints, he was benched for his play. That’s when McCarthy came in and lit up the Saints in the fourth quarter, and he finished with 243 passing yards, one touchdown and an interception. Following the game, Winston was asked about his chances of being the starter for Week 7. “That’s him, that’s a decision that he’ll have to make. What I would love is to just put myself in a better position to execute, and that just starts with me, things I can control,” Winston said. It looks like Harbaugh has gone with the hot hand, and there was always a chance that McCarthy would find some playing time this season. After some rough years with the Minnesota Vikings, the hope is that McCarthy can find new life with the Giants this season and maybe build up his resume so other teams may be interested in him next season. away.headline: New York Giants' Abdul Carter, Andrew Thomas expected to play vs. Saints
away.blurb: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) and linebacker Abdul Carter (calf) are both expected to play despite being listed as questionable. Thomas has managed his groin issue since Week 2 without missing a snap, while Carter’s expected return provides a boost to a defense already without Brian Burns for the season. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) was not addressed by Rapoport. Eluemunor, who suffered the injury in the Week 5 tie against Washington, practiced on a limited basis Friday after missing the prior two days and remains questionable. Head coach John Harbaugh indicated Friday that both tackles were essentially full-go (but were listed as limited) and performed well, though Eluemunor’s status appears less certain and could be a game-time decision. If he is inactive, second-year swing tackle Marcus Mbow would start at right tackle after filling in last week. The Giants also ruled out cornerback Colton Hood (concussion), safety Tyler Nubin (neck) and tight end Theo Johnson (neck). The New York Giants entered Sunday’s Week 6 home game against the New Orleans Saints with encouraging injury news on two key players. Carter has recorded 2.0 sacks and ranks among the league leaders in quarterback pressures. On the other side, Rapoport reported that Saints running back Alvin Kamara (back) and wide receiver Chris Olave (illness) are expected to play as well . With Jameis Winston at quarterback in place of the injured Jaxson Dart, the Giants (3-1-1) will look to protect their lead in the NFC East against a 1-4 Saints team. Availability for Thomas and Carter strengthens their outlook, though the right side of the offensive line remains a variable heading into kickoff. away.blurb: Thomas, who has sat out Wednesday and Thursday over the past several weeks and returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday and Saturday before being cleared to play, is someone to watch this week. Last week he came out of the game just before the big fourth-quarter comeback attempt against the Saints; the veteran left tackle was visibly laboring through his groin injury throughout the game. Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. And with MBow now nursing something, the Giants could be thin at offensive tackle if he can’t play. The Texans have league sack leader Will Anderson, Jr. on one side of their formation and Danielle Hunter on the other. That would be quite the test for rookie J.C. Davis, who would presumably play left tackle; at right tackle, the Giants could potentially move Sisi Mauigoa from right guard to tackle, the position he played in college. Edmunds, Newsome Not Spotted During Media Viewing Portion of Practice Inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) were not spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. If Edmunds can’t go, Micah McFadden would get the start. The question then becomes who would wear the radio in his helmet: rookie Arvell Reese, the most likely candidate, or someone else. Rookie Colton Hood (concussion), receiver Darnell Mooney (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. Paulson Adebo’s Practice Window Opens Cornerback Paulson Adebo’s 21-day practice window is now open. If he clears, he could fill the roster vacancy left after Tuesday’s release of running back Najee Harris and defensive lineman Jihad Ward. Adebo has been on IR since Week 2 with a knee injury and would serve as depth if Newsome doesn’t clear the protocol i

picks.blurb: Broncos at Cardinals preview: Denver aims for three-game win streak - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football WNBA Finals: Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Broncos at Cardinals preview: Denver aims for three-game win streak SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos scrambles against the Seattle Seahawks during an NFL football game at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian St. Clair Wed, October 21, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos are coming off a huge win over the defending Super Bowl champs. Next on the docket is a scrappy Arizona Cardinals bunch that just pulled a huge road upset of the Los Angeles Rams. The good news for the Broncos (4-2) is that they got the mini-bye week before heading to the desert and could get a few players back from injury and the commissioner's exempt list. Denver looks to extend its winning streak to three games after coming out of a gauntlet to start the season. The Broncos are currently -4.5-point road favorites over Arizona (2-4). The total sits at over/under 43.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Denver : Thirty-first in total offense (252.2 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (84.2 YPG), 28th in passing offense (168.0 YPG), 26th in scoring offense (19.0 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total offense (307.3 yards per game), 22nd in rushing offense (96.3 YPG), 20th in passing offense (211.0 YPG), 24th in scoring offense (21.0 points per game). Defensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-second in total defense (348.3 yards per game), 31st in rushing defense (139.8 YPG), 10th in passing defense (208.5 YPG), tied for 10th in scoring defense (20.8 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total defense (350.5 yards per game), 20th in rushing defense (120.8 YPG), 22nd in passing defense (229.7 YPG), tied for 31st in scoring defense (29.7 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the line of scrimmage on offense The Broncos offensive line has been the definition of "meh" to start the regular season. It's nowhere near what it's been the last few seasons, but it also isn't horrid either. Denver needs to dominate the line of scrimmage on Sunday. Open lanes in the running game and do a better job of pass protection. It's a cliche, but success on offense starts in the trenches. Getting that could lay the foundation for jump-starting the offense. — Ian St. Clair Bench Bo Nix; Start Jarrett Stidham Just kidding. Ya'll crazy if you think benching Bo Nix is even remotely the answer. That said, Bo Nix does need to play better, and he isn't seeing the field well to start the season. He's had slow starts in every season he's played, so, for now, I'm chalking this up to another slow start. However, seven games in, I'm hoping to see him take flight a bit now that the hardest part of the Broncos' schedule is complete. At 4-2, they got through it with a winning record, and that is all we could hope for. — Tim Lynch Pressure the QB The key to this game is the same as it has been every week. Get to the QB. The defense has done a great job this season of causing mayhem in the backfield. Make it uncomfortable for Jacoby Brissett (like the back of a Volkswagen). When QBs are harassed and hurried, they make mistakes. — Adam Malnati Disciplined, execution-based offensive football This team needs to execute at a high level, and it will win this game easily. The defense is already there. away.headline: First Week 7 Injury Report Offers Encouragement to Broncos
away.blurb: The team released its first injury report following Wednesday's practice, on which cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss were listed as limited and full participants, respectively. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was considered limited due to an apparent chest injury he picked up amid last Thursday's win over the Seahawks, during which he exited to the locker room. Waddle seems in little danger of missing Week 7. Running back Jonah Coleman, as previously reported , logged a full session after being designated to return from injured reserve. Coleman is expected to be activated to the 53-man roster and play at Arizona. Coleman's services will be required (alongside J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey) with backup RB Tyler Badie nursing a thumb injury, which held him out of Wednesday's practice. Badie will need at least limited sessions on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at playing. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) also did not practice and are unlikely to go Sunday. Elliss is a candidate for IR, though he's anticipated back at some point this season. “He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," Payton told reporters on Wednesday. Although some players, such as Hufanga and wide receiver Pat Bryant (IR), are still unavailable due to injury, the Broncos are beginning to round out into shape at an advantageous time — sitting at 4-2 and having completed the toughest portion of their schedule. The Denver Broncos are getting healthier ahead of their Week 7 road trip to face the Arizona Cardinals. Moss returned from his rib injury last week, but Surtain has been sidelined with an ankle issue he suffered in Week 4. The perennial All-Pro avoided short-term injured reserve and figures to have a chance to play against the Cardinals — though Week 8 versus Kansas City remains his likeliest target date. Veteran Taylor Rapp filled in admirably for Hufanga last week and figures to do so again. Coleman's reinsertion into the lineup will more than make up for the loss of Badie. Elliss' injury is offset by the reinstatement of incumbent starting OLB Jonathon Cooper, who missed the first six games while on the Commissioner's Exempt list. “You never know how it’s going to unfold, but that’s a positive relative to our team. We’ll see how this week goes," Payton said regarding Cooper. All of this, in preparation for a game the Broncos are favored to win by nearly five points. It's been a rollercoaster in the Mile High City thus far, but there's hope that things will soon stabilize. away.blurb: Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain ( ankle ) and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) were limited while safety Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss ( ankle ) and running back Tyler Badie ( thumb ) did not participate. Meanwhile, Cooper is expected to return to the active roster this week after being reinstated by the NFL . Badie injured his thumb in the second quarter of last Thursday's game, and he was ruled out just before halftime. picks.headline: Packers vs. Lions predictions: Detroit's biggest weakness could decide Week 7
picks.blurb: Detroit scores points like no other, but also gives them up at an alarming rate. In other words, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should be salivating at the matchup. The fantasy managers who roster those players will be thinking the same thing. More importantly, this is a key contest in the ever-crowded NFC North where there is no margin for error. Green Bay enters the contest at 4-2, erasing any negative thoughts that surfaced after the 0-2 start to the year. Detroit is 3-2, which is good enough for last place in the NFC North. Both teams are chasing the 5-0 Vikings , with the 4-2 Bears standing in the way as well. With only so many playoff spots to go around, this Week 7 matchup could have massive implications down the road. Here's a look at the keys to the game, injuries to watch and a prediction. Lions vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions -2.5 Moneyline: Lions -142; Packers +120 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions Keys To Victory Slow down Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. It's easier said than done, of course, but it's the one true path to victory for Detroit - outside of winning a shootout. The Lions' secondary has been a huge weakness all season long, and perhaps there is no better team position to exploit that than the Packers. Green Bay will try to hit some home runs with its speedy receivers. Even with Brian Branch set to return, Detroit will have to be willing to sit back in zone coverage and hold the visitors to some singles. Packers Keys To Victory Stay patient. With a defense as weak as the Lions, the Packers just have to play the waiting game. And that's something Dan Campbell's teams haven't been known to do. Detroit can either take away the long ball or attempt to get to Jordan Love with pressure. If the Lions sit back, then the Packers need to show an ability to run the ball. If they pressure, get ready to light up the scoreboard. Green Bay has the advantage, but it can't beat itself. Injuries to watch • S Brian Branch • OL Cade Mays • OL Aaron Banks. Lions vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 34, Lions 30 This game might come down to who has the ball last. Detroit might be coming out of the bye with some reinforcements, but this is still a defense that will ruin a season. And for that reason, no lead is safe - especially against the rival Packers, who can strike quickly. Jordan Love was forced to grow up as a quarterback without a running game to rely on through the first six weeks. He is passing that test with flying colors after a slow start. Trust the more well-rounded Packers to get the job done and push their winning streak to four. Adam Kaufman: Lions 31, Packers 27 This should be fun. Green Bay has won three straight, but Detroit comes out of its bye with reinforcements. Brian Branch's expected return won't magically fix the secondary, though even a few additional stops could make a significant difference. The Lions already have an offense capable of taking advantage, with Jahmyr Gibbs headlining their weapons. Jordan Love should still find opportunities, and the Packers can absolutely win if they protect him and avoid giving the home team extra possessions. Josh Jacobs' availability is another important piece. I'm expecting both quarterbacks to have productive stretches. But Jared Goff and Dan Campbell have been a dynamic duo with extended rest and know what's at stake in a crowded NFC North. This should be competitive well into the fourth quarter, but I like the Lions indoors. picks.headline: Packers vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 7
picks.blurb: The NFC North still looks like one of the NFL’s most competitive divisions just six weeks into the 2026 season. Every team in the division finished with a winning record in 2025, and that trend has continued into this year . Now the Packers and Lions are gearing up for a huge divisional matchup that could have huge ramifications come playoff time. Green Bay is looking strong after a questionable start to the season. They are on a three-game winning streak after taking care of Dallas on Sunday Night Football . The Packers are still a bit behind the Vikings, but getting a win in Week 7 will get them one step closer to catching up. Meanwhile, Detroit quieted their doubters in Week 5 after crushing Arizona in the desert. The Lions even got a solid game from their defense, something that has eluded them for most of the season. But Detroit is coming off their bye week, so it is impossible to know if they’ll carry over that momentum or come out flat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Which team will come out on top in this massive divisional matchup? Here are three bold predictions before the NFC North clash between the Lions and Packers in Week 7. Jared Goff throws his first interception of the season, but still shreds Packers defense Goff may be the most underrated quarterback in the entire NFL this season. He may look like a quarterback from a different age, but Goff can still sling it with the best of them. Detroit’s franchise quarterback has 1,485 passing yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions through five games. That’s right, he still has not thrown an interception at any point this season. This speaks to how careful Goff is with the football, no doubt owing to his veteran experience. All of that said, this could be the week that the streak comes to an end. The Lions should not underestimate the Packers’ defensive unit, even if they don’t have Micah Parsons in Week 7. Green Bay has one of the better coverage units in the NFL this season despite an unproven cornerback room. Even more impressive is that they lead the NFL in interceptions with nine through the first six games. If any team is going to snap Goff’s streak, it will be the packers. Goff will throw his first interception of the season against Green Bay on Sunday. All good things must come to an end, including his impressive streak of clean games. However, that doesn’t mean he’ll wilt against the Packers. Detroit will finish this game with at least 400 passing yards, shredding Green Bay’s secondary from wire to wire. Josh Jacobs rumbles for 100 rushing yards, two touchdowns in 2026 debut Green Bay’s one weakness this season has been their rushing attack. The Packers are averaging a pitiful 59.8 rushing yards per game this season. That is due to a combination of offensive line issues and a thin running back group. But the latter is about to change. Josh Jacobs looks slated to return in Week 7 after being removed from the commissioner’s exempt list. “I would say Jacobs has been preliminarily cleared and is expected to play this week. He is going to practice. He’s going to be on the field. They say he has kept in good shape, and the Green Bay Packers, who have had a really solid start to the season, probably could use a little bit of an improved running game, and they get Josh Jacobs in Week 7 to come in and do it,” NFL insider Ian Rapoport said on Wednesday via Good Morning Football. Getting Jacobs back won’t fix everything overnight. After all, it is fair to be skeptical of how ready he truly is after staying away from football for over a month. Still, Jacobs could have a breakout game against Detroit if Matt LaFleur dials up enough carries for him. Jacobs will go over 100 rushing yards and score two touchdowns against the Lions. Green Bay wins an NFC North shootout thanks to Detroit’s compromised defense Of course, the matchup that everyone will be watching in this one is Jordan Love against Detroit’s struggling secondary. Green Bay suddenly looks capable of keeping up with Detroit’s offense. The emergence of both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden has unlocked the team’s passing attack. On paper, they’re in the same tier as Detroit in terms of passing yards per game. The good news for the Lions is that Brian Branch is expected to make his 2026 debut against the Packers in Week 7. It is impossible to know just how good Branch will look after last season’s Achilles injury . Getting him back is also no guarantee that Detroit’s defense will magically play better. But it is a start. In the long term, getting Branch back should do wonders for the Lions. Unfortunately, it won’t be enough to win this game. The Packers win by one score in an epic shootout at Ford Field. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. LaFleur has been noncommittal about the three-time Pro Bowler's availability in Detroit. Time will tell whether this is just gamesmanship. Jacob's presence (or lack thereof) looms large for a Packers group that has been unable to get anything going on the ground . They're the only squad averaging fewer than three yards per carry (2.9) and rank dead last in rushing yards per game (59.8) Does Kevin Zeitler finally plug in at RG? Zeitler, 36, signed with the Packers on Sept. 30 and has notably been active in each of their past two matches. He's been limited to special teams duties so far; however, the 15-year veteran is expected to take over at right guard in due course. Now that he's had time to get his sea legs in Green Bay, why not give Zeitler the nod in the Motor City? His rock-solid decade-plus-long career includes a pit stop with the Lions in 2024. Lions set to get much-needed reinforcements Lions starting center Cade Mays and Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch are set to make their 2026 debuts, barring any setbacks. The former was brought in as a free agent this offseason on a three-year, $25 million contract and got hurt in training camp. Meanwhile, the latter should instantly help address a secondary that has struggled mightily. 3 Predictions for Packers vs. Lions 1. Packers still don't get a 50+ yard rusher (even with Josh Jacobs) Detroit has surrendered the seventh-fewest rushing yards to opposing RBs through six games (422). They're low-key giving up the 11th-most yards per carry to backs (4.26), though their defense has been hemorrhaging yards through the air, as highlighted below. That should translate to another big day for Love and Co., so Jacobs and the running back room probably won't need to do much. 2. Tucker Kraft scores two TDs No team has surrendered more receptions (51), receiving yards (545) and touchdowns (nine) to tight ends than the Lions. Everyone knows this has been a blind spot for them, too, as evidenced by their league-high target share allowed to the position. Enter Kraft, who's slowly but surely rounding into form as he gets further removed from his torn right ACL last November. Kraft has posted five-plus targets and receptions in three straight contests. He's also been a factor near the end zone, recording at least one inside-the-20 look in four consecutive outings. It's easy to envision him finding pay dirt — more than once. 3. Packers find a way to win on the road Green Bay's starting to find its groove on both sides of the ball. Love is operating at a high level, and their stop unit has been a revelation under defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon. They're equipped to exploit the Lions' weaknesses and keep the good times rolling with a fourth successive victory. Packers 30, Lions 23. picks.headline: Packers add Cowboys former first-round pick before Lions game
picks.blurb: The Green Bay Packers defeated the Dallas Cowboys by a 23-13 final score in their Week 6 matchup. Now, the Packers have added one of the Cowboys’ former first-round picks after defeating them in their last game. According to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky , the Packers have signed former Cowboys defensive tackle Mazi Smith to their practice squad ahead of their Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions. This was shortly after Smith tried out for Green Bay. With this move, the Packers have added another defensive tackle with NFL experience to their depth in Smith. There is no harm in the Packers taking a chance on the former first-round pick, and he will now be aiming to impress on their practice squad. If he does, perhaps it could lead to him being elevated to their active roster soon. Smith was selected by the Cowboys in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft, 26th overall. In 43 career NFL games over four seasons split between the Cowboys, New York Jets, and Miami Dolphins, he has recorded 2.0 sacks to go along with 57 combined tackles. It will now be interesting to see if Smith can get into game action with the Packers after landing on their practice squad from here. away.blurb: Here’s some good news: receiver Savion Williams (ankle) had his practice window with the team open up last week and was a limited participant on Wednesday, along with defensive lineman Jordon Riley — who began to practice with the team much sooner than expected from his 2025 season-ending Achilles injury. It’s probably hard to count on Riley jumping up to the active roster with just one week of practice under his belt, but at least he’s trending in a positive direction. It seems much more likely that Williams would be activated this week to help replace Skyy Moore’s reps on offense and in the return game. For what it’s worth, Moore was seen in a boot after his ankle injury on Sunday and on a scooter on Wednesday . It wouldn’t be out of left field for him to land on the injured reserve, based on the little we know about his injury — if the team needs the numbers. Notably, the Packers went out of their way to sign a second practice squad cornerback on Monday, the first time all year that the team has had two at the position. Green Bay has been pretty thin at defensive back this year, from a numbers perspective, a result of the team being “oversigned” at the offensive line, defensive line and tight end positions for 2026 on the full 70-man roster (potentially at running back and edge defender, too, depending on your definition). For the most part, my injury analysis this season has basically boiled down to “next man up on the 53-man roster.” The Green Bay Packers’ cluster of injuries has mostly hit two units, the offensive and defensive lines — where the team has been over-signed since they made their initial active roster — leaving them without needing to call players up from the practice squad. The two exceptions so far have been the promotion of running back Pierre Strong Jr. (for Chris Brooks, who went on IR) and linebacker Kristian Welch (for Edgerrin Cooper, who went on IR). This week, though, the Packers’ active roster might be stress-tested beyond a one-off injury at a position for the first time. away.blurb: But there are some concerns at the moment regarding the statuses of some of their key players, including quarterback Jordan Love and wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . All three appeared on Green Bay’s injury report on Wednesday with limited practice participation labels . The Green Bay Packers are on a roll as they enter Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season on a three-game winning streak following a 23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys over the weekend. Love said that he is dealing with a sore back, but he allayed fears on his availability for Week 7’s game against the Detroit Lions by saying that there’s no chance he’ll not suit up for that contest against an NFC North rival, per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. Meanwhile, the statuses of Watson and Golden also don’t seem to be something to be overly concerned about, at least for now. Watson and Golden have been Love’s top targets downfield in the 2026 season. The 27-year-old Watson is leading the Packers with 538 receiving yards to go with six touchdowns on 29 receptions and 48 targets. The speedy Golden, on the other hand, is having a breakout campaign. The 23-year-old former Texas Longhorns star wideout has 501 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 30 catches and 57 targets to his name through six weeks of football. Given how bad the Lions’ pass defense has been thus far in the 2026 season, Green Bay has a great opportunity to showcase their passing attack. Detroit is allowing 297.4 passing yards per game — the worst in the NFL. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. Meanwhile, the statuses of Watson and Golden also don’t seem to be something to be overly concerned about, at least for now. Watson and Golden have been Love’s top targets downfield in the 2026 season. The 27-year-old Watson is leading the Packers with 538 receiving yards to go with six touchdowns on 29 receptions and 48 targets. The speedy Golden, on the other hand, is having a breakout campaign. The 23-year-old former Texas Longhorns star wideout has 501 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 30 catches and 57 targets to his name through six weeks of football. Given how bad the Lions’ pass defense has been thus far in the 2026 season, Green Bay has a great opportunity to showcase their passing attack. picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football WNBA Finals: Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III | Chris Unger/GettyImages Cody Williams Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:15 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. away.headline: Rams Week 7 Injury Report: More Bad News as Trent McDuffie, Nate Landman Face Uncertainty
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are preparing to play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, and the injuries just keep piling up. Earlier this week , the Rams placed wide receiver Davante Adams and nose tackle Poona Ford on injured reserve. Additionally, defensive lineman Kobie Turner has been ruled out for a handful of weeks. "Trent will be a DNP with his groin. We'll take it a day at a time, like what I told you guys, and evaluate his status as we go," said head coach Sean McVay. "Then on Monday, found out Landman landed in the concussion protocol so he'll be a DNP." While Landman's presence on the injury report isn't surprising given that he's been there the last few weeks, his placement in the concussion protocol is certainly a new development. In order to return to play, Landman will be limited in his allowed activity. He'll then graduate to an aerobic exercise program overseen by the club's medical staff. Lastly, after leaving Kobie Turner off the injured reserve transactions on Tuesday alongside Davante Adams and Poona Ford, the Rams placed him on injured reserve Wednesday. Turner will be out for a minimum of four weeks. In corresponding moves, the Rams signed EDGE Darryl Peterson III to the active roster and signed Jalen Hunt to the practice squad. "Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever and they're like, 'I have to trade a guy in and out now.' We're like, 'Well, that guy has worked his ass off for the last eight months to get this opportunity and it's unfortunate he doesn't get to do what he loves to do,'" said quarterback Matthew Stafford. "I feel more for our guys than I do for anybody else.I know the work that they put into it to be out here doing what they love, so that hurts me for them. But at the same time, I think I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win." For the Raiders, defensive lineman Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant as he remains in the concussion protocol. The Rams will certainly monitor the statuses of tight end Brock Bowers, offensive tackle Kolton Miller, and linebacker Quay Walker. All three were limited on Wednesday. away.headline: New NFL trade rumors on potential Rams deal for WR after Davante Adams' injury
away.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . After placing star receiver Davante Adams on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury, the Los Angeles Rams reportedly will be looking for a replacement. ESPN's Dan Graziano reported that the Rams are expected to scour the trade market for a wide receiver in hopes of salvaging their season. "I do not expect the Rams to go down without a fight, and my understanding is that they will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver in the wake of the Davante Adams injury," Graziano stated. "The issue, of course, is that they don't have a ton to trade." This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

away.headline: Rams aren’t rushing to replace Davante Adams despite major injury blow
away.blurb: Adams was just one of the many casualties to land on the injury report this week as the team announced on Monday that nose tackle Poona Ford (ruptured triceps), and kicker Blake Grupe (torn ACL) would be out for the remainder of the season . The Los Angeles Rams have a hole at the wide receiver position but don’t appear to be worried about it. Head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Wednesday that the team hasn’t spoken internally about bringing in another wide receiver, as they’re set to be without Davante Adams for the next 6-10 weeks. “That’s not something that we’ve talked about right now,” McVay said to Rams team reporter Stu Jackson. “We’ve got some depth on our roster. Maybe we talked about the practice squad, but not anything external.” After Adams and Puka Nacua proved to be one of the best wide receiver duos in football last season, they will likely spend at least half of this season not playing alongside each other. Nacua missed the Rams Week 2 and Week 3 games against the Giants and Broncos due to a groin injury . Los Angeles finally had their prime duo together until the Rams’ final drive in their 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, when Adams suffered a semitendinosus rupture. “Obviously with Tae going down, everybody’s going to get more opportunities,” Quarterback Matthew Stafford said to Jackson. Stafford went on to praise second-year wide receiver, Konata Mumpfield, as a potential replacement for Adams, as he called him, “a guy that has had some [chances] and done a nice job with them. He’s going to continue to grow. He’s, again, young in his journey as a player in the NFL. He’s a really talented kid.” Stafford continued on to say that Mumpfield soaks it all in and the team is looking for him to do his best. The team will also be without star defensive end Kobie Turner as he will miss the next 4-6 weeks due to a groin injury. While Los Angeles will be without Adams for an extended period, this season is also a contract year for him, as he will be hitting the open market after he signed a two-year, $44 million contract with the team in March, 2025.

(AP Photo/Geneva Heffernan) (AP Photo/Geneva Heffernan) 1 / 2 Chargers Chiefs Football Chargers Chiefs Football Seahawks Broncos Football Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kenneth Walker III is going back to Seattle with the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs to face the team he helped lead to the Super Bowl last season. Walker, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs visit the Seahawks (3-3) on Sunday night. Walker leads the NFL in rushing with 665 yards despite already taking a bye week while the Seattle has missed the Super Bowl MVP. The Seahawks are 18th in rushing and have averaged 3.9 yards per attempt. Sam Darnold has seven interceptions in slightly more than four games and the Seahawks haven't made up for Walker's absence. But they have Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who leads the NFL with 717 receiving yards and seven touchdowns. Walker has provided the Chiefs a balanced attack. They haven't had a 1,000-yard rusher since Mahomes became the starter in 2018. Walker is on pace for 2,261 yards, which would set a single-season record. Despite their struggles, the Seahawks are 2 ½-point favorites. Pro Picks likes the home team. SEAHAWKS: 23-20 NEW ENGLAND (4-2) at CHICAGO (4-2) Line: Bears minus 3 Drake Maye has led the banged-up Patriots to three straight wins. A.J. Brown returned last week but dropped three passes. Caleb Williams was nearly flawless in his first game back, leading the Bears to 31 points. Chicago plays consecutive primetime games against last season's Super Bowl opponents, starting with the Thursday night matchup. PITTSBURGH (4-2) vs. NEW ORLEANS (2-4), in Paris Line: Steelers minus 3 Aaron Rodgers led the Steelers back from a 13-point deficit in Tampa Bay, relying on DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard. The Saints got their run game going in a win over the Giants. Both teams are spending the week in Paris before playing the NFL's first regular-season game there. The Steelers have covered the spread four of the past five games. STEELERS: 23-18 CINCINNATI (3-2) at BALTIMORE (4-2) Line: Ravens minus 2 ½ Joe Burrow and the Bengals are coming off a bye. Their defense had a great start but has struggled against the run in the past three games. The Ravens still might not have Lamar Jackson so Tyler Huntley would start his third straight game. Baltimore is eighth in rushing and relying on Derrick Henry is a smart move if Jackson is out. BENGALS: 22-17 CLEVELAND (4-2) at TENNESSEE (1-5) Line: Browns minus 1 ½ Deshaun Watson led another fourth-quarter game-winning drive for the Browns, but the offense has struggled despite the team's winning record. Tennessee's offense is last in the NFL. The Titans beat the Colts for their first win, but Cam Ward had another rough outing. UPSET SPECIAL: TITANS: 20-17 INDIANAPOLIS (2-4) at MINNESOTA (5-0) Line: Vikings minus 6 1/2 The Colts' struggles cost general manager Chris Ballard his job. Coach Shane Steichen is clearly on the hottest of seats and the team has to find ways to win. The undefeated Vikings are coming off a bye. They've been winning on defense and special teams and need Kyler Murray to get the offense going. VIKINGS: 23-18 Line: Jets minus 4 ½ The Jets haven't won an AFC East game under coach Aaron Glenn, going 0-7. They have their best chance this week vs. Miami. The winless Dolphins are coming off a bye. QB Malik Willis has the worst passer rating (68.4) among starters. Line: Texans minus 10 ½ J.J. McCarthy is replacing Jameis Winston, who had a winning record after taking over for Jaxson Dart. McCarthy will face an underachieving defense stacked with talent. C.J. Stroud is playing great football for the Texans, who've won two in a row. TEXANS: 26-17 SAN FRANCISCO (6-0) at ATLANTA (2-4) Line: 49ers minus 3 ½ Christian McCaffrey vs. Bijan Robinson in a matchup of All-Pro backs who are close friends and train together. The undefeated 49ers keep winning despite losing key players because they have Brock Purdy. The Falcons lost two games to start the season, won two in a row and have now lost two straight. Atlanta is 3-2 ATS in past five games against San Francisco. TAMPA BAY (1-5) at CAROLINA (3-2) Line: Panthers minus 3 ½ Baker Mayfield is aiming to return for the Buccaneers, who have lost 12 of their past 15 games. The Bucs have played tough defense but their offense is among the bottom third. Bryce Young is playing his best football for the Panthers. He has 11 TDs and only two picks. PANTHERS: 23-20 DENVER (4-2) at ARIZONA (2-4) Line: Broncos minus 4 ½ Bo Nix is taking plenty of heat despite Denver's winning record. Nix and the offense have to get on track. The Broncos have faced a tough schedule that doesn't get easier after Arizona. The Cardinals beat the Rams on the road last week and have to carry that momentum into a difficult matchup. BRONCOS: 24-16 GREEN BAY (4-2) at DETROIT (3-2) Line: Lions minus 3 The Packers have won three in a row, the defense has been stout and Josh Jacobs is coming back to boost the offense with Micah Parsons working toward his return. The Lions have the league's worst defense that's sometimes offset by a prolific offense. This one should be a shootout. Line: Rams minus 4 ½ The Rams haven't played close to Super Bowl favorites. And, injuries are piling up with Davante Adams now going down for several weeks. But they still have Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua and Aaron Donald. The Raiders have lost three in a row but Kirk Cousins is playing well so hold off on Fernando Mendoza. A defense that's allowed 30-plus points three straight games has been the problem. BEST BET: RAMS: 31-20 DALLAS (2-4) at PHILADELPHIA (2-4) Line: Cowboys minus 4 ½ The Cowboys have an opportunity in a wide-open NFC East, but have had issues on defense and now a dynamic offense has sputtered. The Eagles are reeling and won't have Jalen Hurts likely for the rest of the season. Tanner McKee makes his second straight start for Philadelphia. COWBOYS: 24-23 Last week: Straight up: 8-6.
