picks.headline: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams
picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football WNBA Finals: Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III | Chris Unger/GettyImages Cody Williams Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:15 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs trade acquisition in line for his first start as offensive line injuries linger into first practice for Week 7 vs. Seahawks
away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs could trot out a third starting offensive line combination of the 2026 NFL season in Seattle. Wednesday's practice offered few encouraging signs for a pair of injured tackles. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid confirmed Wednesday that starting right tackle Jaylon Moore remains in the NFL's concussion protocol . Moore must clear the league's return-to-play protocols to suit up against the Seahawks. According to Reid, he would not participate in Wednesday's practice. What Are the NFL's Return-to-Play Protocols for Concussions? Players placed in the NFL concussion protocol must complete five phases without symptoms before they can be cleared to return to play. Symptom-limited activity: Light stretching and stationary bike riding. It remains to be seen whether Moore can clear those protocols ahead of the Week 7 matchup. However, sitting out of practice entirely on Wednesday isn't a good start. So who is in line to start at right tackle? Fans would hope starting left tackle Josh Simmons could return to the lineup after he practiced in a limited capacity ahead of Week 6's game against the Los Angeles Chargers. That didn't look promising on Wednesday. Reporters didn't spot Simmons on the field during their brief look at team stretch and warm-ups. Reid also didn't mention Simmons' status when he addressed injured players. He spoke only about Moore and wide receiver Rashee Rice, who also did not practice. Simmons did return to practice in a limited capacity last week. Still, clips captured during the brief window the team gives media members ahead of practice made it clear Simmons wasn't 100%. He was seen grimacing while stretching , and he simply didn't look right while jogging on the field. It very much looks like the back injury will keep him out longer. Reid's comments on Monday suggested the Chiefs are continuing to work through his back issue while ramping up his workload. Again, missing practice Wednesday doesn't set him up for a likely Week 7 return. away.headline: Chiefs Injury Report: Latest on Rashee Rice, Josh Simmons, Jaylon Moore Ahead of Primetime Showdown in Seattle
away.blurb: Simmons returned to practice in a limited capacity last week as a part of his recovery and ramp-up process from his back injury— later described as a bulging disc —that first appeared late in training camp . Simmons participated in all three practices last week but was a limited participant each time. Moore left Sunday's win over the Los Angeles Chargers due to a concussion that kept him out for the game's second half . While Moore navigates the concussion protocol, offensive lineman Joshua Ezeudu is expected to be the first man up at right tackle, as he finished the game in Moore's place against LA. The Chiefs made a flurry of linebacker-based roster moves on Wednesday, designating linebacker Cooper McDonald to return to practice after a short stint on the injured reserve list. McDonald was placed on IR due to a knee injury suffered early in KC's Week 1 win over the Denver Broncos. Ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs' Week 7 showdown against the Seattle Seahawks , the team has a mixed bag of injury news. On Wednesday, head coach Andy Reid indicated that wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring) and right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) would not practice today, while left tackle Josh Simmons (back) is expected to participate to some extent. Rice suffered a hamstring injury in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders and has been sidelined since. Even with the benefit of the team's Week 5 bye, Rice was not ready to practice in the team's lead-up to Week 6. "Rashee's getting better as we go, by the day, so that helps," Reid said on Wednesday. Cooper McDonald returns to practice, others shuffled The Chiefs also signed linebacker Aiden Fisher to the practice squad, adding the rookie seventh-round draft pick to their developmental plans. Fisher played for James Madison and Indiana before being drafted by the Houston Texans in April. In corresponding moves, the team waived linebacker Cam Jones and terminated the practice squad contract of running back Nate Carter. The Seattle Seahawks received one of their most encouraging injury updates of the season on Wednesday, October 21. Running back Zach Charbonnet was listed as a full participant on Seattle's first injury report ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs , marking another significant step in his recovery from a torn ACL. But before Charbonnet can make his season debut, Seattle must make an important roster decision. Zach Charbonnet Injury Update Comes Before Critical Seahawks Deadline The Seahawks opened Charbonnet's 21-day practice window on October 1, allowing him to resume football activities while remaining on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. That window reaches its conclusion on Thursday, October 22, meaning Seattle must activate Charbonnet to its 53-man roster or leave him on the PUP list for the remainder of the season. “Zach is going to have a full week's worth of reps, so that's exciting, and there's a possibility that you could see him on Sunday in some capacity, so that's exciting,” Macdonald said during his October 19 press conference, according to the team's official website. The latest injury report strengthens the case for Charbonnet's availability, although full participation does not guarantee that he will play Sunday. Seahawks Could Get Much-Needed Help at Running Back Against Chiefs Rookie running back Jadarian Price remains on injured reserve after suffering a chest injury, leaving the Seahawks to rely heavily on Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. Wednesday's full-participation designation is particularly encouraging because Charbonnet had previously been limited as the Seahawks gradually increased his workload. Head coach Mike Macdonald had already indicated that the running back might return against Kansas City. Charbonnet's potential return comes at an important time for Seattle's rushing attack. Those numbers help explain why Seattle could benefit from having him available near the goal line, especially as the offense searches for more consistency. The Seahawks also received a potentially encouraging development along the offensive line, with starting right guard Anthony Bradford returning to practice this week. Bradford was listed as limited Wednesday while working toward his own return from injured reserve. The Seattle Seahawks received one of their most encouraging injury updates of the season on Wednesday, October 21. Running back Zach Charbonnet was listed as a full participant on Seattle's first injury report ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs , marking another significant step in his recovery from a torn ACL. But before Charbonnet can make his season debut, Seattle must make an important roster decision. Zach Charbonnet Injury Update Comes Before Critical Seahawks Deadline The Seahawks opened Charbonnet's 21-day practice window on October 1, allowing him to resume football activities while remaining on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. That window reaches its conclusion on Thursday, October 22, meaning Seattle must activate Charbonnet to its 53-man roster or leave him on the PUP list for the remainder of the season. “Zach is going to have a full week's worth of reps, so that's exciting, and there's a possibility that you could see him on Sunday in some capacity, so that's exciting,” Macdonald said during his October 19 press conference, according to the team's official website. The latest injury report strengthens the case for Charbonnet's availability, although full participation does not guarantee that he will play Sunday. Seahawks Could Get Much-Needed Help at Running Back Against Chiefs Rookie running back Jadarian Price remains on injured reserve after suffering a chest injury, leaving the Seahawks to rely heavily on Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. Charbonnet would bring a proven scoring threat to that rotation. During the 2025 regular season, the former UCLA standout recorded 730 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns on 184 carries across 16 games. home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks are looking to snap their current two-game losing streak this weekend against the Kansas City Chiefs, and they may have some much-needed reinforcements coming their way. On Wednesday, the Seahawks released their injury report for practice, and there is an incredibly welcome development: running back Zach Charbonnet is a full participant! Charbonnet has been working hard to get back on the field after he suffered an ACL injury in the Divisional Round last season. Now it appears he is on track to make his 2026 debut. If he does, he will take the field against his former running mate in the backfield in Kenneth Walker III, who will be on the other sideline playing for the Kansas City Chiefs. Before the season started, this looked like a potential swing game for the NFC East standings, but a lot has changed in six weeks. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Here’s a look at the odds, the latest movement since Sunday night and a quick preview of this primetime matchup. Cowboys vs. Eagles Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Cowboys -4.5 (-112) Eagles +4.5 (-108) Cowboys: -225 44.5 (Over -110/Under -110) Dallas opened as a 5.5-point favorite for Monday night’s showdown , but that line has quickly shifted towards the Eagles. Even with Jalen Hurts on injured reserve and out for the season, Philly has a shot to pull off an upset against a Dallas defense that is 31st in the NFL EPA/Play. Plus, the Cowboys’ offense looked awful on Sunday night in a loss to Green Bay, which may have caused the move in this line on Monday morning. Cowboys vs. Eagles Betting Preview The Eagles have covered the spread just once in the 2026 season (in their London loss to Jacksonville), so it’s hard to justify betting on them with a backup at quarterback. However, Dallas’ defense remains a bottom three unit in the league, and McKee (215 passing yards in Week 6) was at least able to move the Philly offense. If Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is able to return in Week 7, it could flip these odds even further towards the Eagles. Dallas needs to figure things out on offense, as Prescott has struggled with turnovers (not all his fault) in the last few games while the offensive line allowed him to take a ton of big hits in Week 6. A win for Philly could bump it back up into at least the No. 3 spot in the odds to win the NFC East, but it seems pretty clear that oddsmakers expect Dallas to eventually figure things out and advance as the division winner. Bettors may want to consider the OVER (44.5) with how poor the Dallas defense has been this season. The OVER is 4-2 in Dallas’ six games and 3-3 in the Eagles’ matchup in 2026. away.headline: 2 Cowboys miss Thursday practice, DeMarvion Overshown progressing in new injury report
away.blurb: The good news for Dallas is that starting linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is making progress and taking a step toward returning to the field, while veteran linebacker Von Miller also returned after a rest day and cornerback Ameer Speed was upgraded to limited. Cowboys Injury Roundup: Two Key Players Eyeing Thursday Return A new week of NFL action officially kicks off on Thursday night in primetime, marking exactly one week since the last time we saw the Dallas Cowboys on the field . Last Thursday did not go as planned for Dallas, as the team suffered an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home, but the team gets an opportunity to bounce back in Week 6 with another primetime showdown. This weekend, Dallas will make the trip to Lambeau Field for a Sunday night showdown with the Green Bay Packers . On Thursday afternoon, the Cowboys returned to the practice field and dropped their latest injury report . On Wednesday, five players did not participate in practice, but on Thursday, that number was down to two. A full look at the team's Week 6 injury report can be seen below. Dallas Cowboys Week 6 Injury Report - Thursday The two players who did not participate in Thursday afternoon's practice are cornerback Cobie Durant and offensive tackle Drew Shelton, who are both dealing with hamstring injuries. Along with Overshown, Miller, and Speed improving their participation statuses on Thursday, there was another player who took a positive step forward: star cornerback Joey Porter Jr., whose home debut was spoiled last week after a sudden illness. But after some extra time to recover from the issues that left him throwing up in the locker room before getting sent home, he is feeling well and on track to play on Sunday night. Porter was listed on Wednesday's report with an ankle issue, but it is not serious and he will be in line for an increased workload this week. home.headline: Eagles not punished by NFL for handling of Jalen Hurts blood clots, per reports; NFLPA says more investigation needed
home.blurb: It was revealed Monday that Hurts will be out indefinitely after multiple clots were discovered in his lungs. The news came two days after Hurts was placed on injured reserve — despite initial reports stating the team wouldn’t place him on IR — and four days after last week’s announcement that he had a blood clot in his calf. “I fully trust the people that are involved in helping us all make these decisions,” Sirianni said. “We have great people here. … The same doctors and trainers that helped 21 of our 22 starters be available in the Super Bowl are the same guys today that deeply care about our guys to help them. “Don’t have much more to say about that. That’s why we put the statement out. Full trust in those guys … kind of feels like you’re questioning that, and I know you guys have a job to do, but I’ve got the relationship with the players that I have because of the time that we spend together and because of the care that we have for each other. So, it’s always at the forefront of our mind.” The Eagles won’t face any heat from the NFL for their handling of Jalen Hurts’ potentially season-ending injury. The NFL concluded, in news first reported by The Athletic and later confirmed by the Associated Press, that the Eagles clearing Hurts to play in Week 5 despite having a superficial blood clot in his calf was “handled appropriately.” The league will not be issuing any punishment for their handling of the medical process, or for Hurts not being given an injury designation for the game. Later on Tuesday, the NFL Players Association issued a statement: “The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.” The Eagles’ medical staff has faced scrutiny from fans and media for its handling of the Hurts situation. Coach Nick Sirianni gave the team’s medical staff a vote of confidence Monday but declined to expand on the specifics of Hurts’ injury process. ©2026 The Philadelphia Inquirer. Visit inquirer.com.
